summary: Research Steam data APIs, legal, UX benchmarks and 2026 stack for GameAgenda; adversarially verify critical claims

researches.label: catalog enumeration
researches.summary:
Keyless full list is gone: ISteamApps/GetAppList v1+v2 vanished from Valve's public API listing on 2025-11-13 (SteamTracking diff), breakage reported from 2025-11-16, now HTTP 404; Valve docs say use IStoreService/GetAppList. That endpoint is documented, needs any Web API key (a user key works on api.steampowered.com; partner.steam-api.com needs a publisher key), pages in appid order via last_appid/have_more_results, max_results 50k (default 10k), flags include_games (default)/dlc/software/videos/hardware (no demos/music/mods) and supports if_modified_since deltas. Real output (jsnli daily dump, 2026-10-27): 196,595 games (~20 MB = 4 calls), 63,919 DLC; rows {appid,name,last_modified,price_change_number}; base names, not localized; coming-soon, free and adult-only games included; delisted games excluded; regional SKUs included; churn ~3.3k games/day. A key needs a non-limited account (>= US$5 spent) + Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator; ToU: 100k calls/day, key confidential, licence 'specific to your Application' -> one server-side key; sync needs ~45 calls/day.
Live-tested today WITHOUT key: IStoreQueryService/Query (undocumented) gives up to 1000 ids/call, deep offsets OK, sort=2 = ascending appid, filters released_only/coming_soon_only/type/content descriptors. Totals now: 317,807 store apps; 196,617 games = 133,880 released + 62,681 coming soon; 63,079 DLC; 43,376 demos; 11,595 soundtracks; 2,919 software; 9,674 adult-only. IStoreBrowseService/GetItems (keyless) gives localized names, type, coming-soon/early-access/release date, content descriptors and unlisted:true for delisted games (appdetails still says success:true). SearchSuggestions/storesearch are keyless typeahead fallbacks. No CORS headers -> Steam calls must be server-side. Throttling undocumented (community: ~120 req/5 min/IP). SteamSpy only as popularity signal; PICS is complete but heavy and ToS-gray; SteamDB has no API and forbids scraping.
Plan: keyed GetAppList backbone (games only for MVP) + keyless GetItems/Query enrichment + soft-delete/unlisted tracking + ~1.9 MB (brotli) client-side name index for instant search; keyless Query pass as feature-flagged fallback. Raw probes: C:\Users\lucas\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-lucas-Documents-Programacion-GameAgenda\56497ade-bd80-409d-8199-9f2b9ba10c3e\scratchpad\research\R1\

findings.claim: ISteamApps/GetAppList v1 and v2 were removed from Valve's public Web API listing on 2025-11-13 and now return HTTP 404; no dated Valve announcement exists.
findings.details: SteamTracking (automated dump of api.steampowered.com GetSupportedAPIList) commit 1978dcc003 at 2025-11-13T22:05:17Z deleted both GetAppList v1 and v2 entries from API/ISteamApps.json. First breakage report found: SteamAutoCracker #107 opened 2025-11-16; maintainer on 2025-12-01: 'It seems that Steam killed the endpoint'. woctezuma/steam-store-snapshots says deprecated 'as of November 25, 2025'. Steamworks page only says 'Deprecated - this API can no longer scale to the number of items available on Steam. Please use IStoreService/GetAppList instead.' (undated). Live 2026-10-28: 404 'Method GetAppList not found in interface ISteamApps' (v1 also 404 per community).

findings.claim: Valve documents IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 as the replacement: key (required, any Web API key) plus optional if_modified_since, have_description_language, include_games (default on), include_dlc/software/videos/hardware, last_appid and max_results (default 10k, max 50k).
findings.details: Official: 'Returns a list of all apps available on the Steam Store'; 'By default only "Game" items will be returned'; 'The results are returned in order of appid' and next calls 'should pass the last appid returned by the previous request as the last_appid parameter'. include_videos = 'videos and series'. have_description_language only FILTERS (apps having a description in that language). There are no include_demos/include_music/include_mods flags, so demos, soundtracks and mods cannot be listed here (fine for a to-play list). Same parameter list in SteamTracking's public API dump and xPaw docs. Docs show host partner.steam-api.com (see R1-04).

findings.claim: The response is {response:{apps:[{appid,name,last_modified,price_change_number}],have_more_results,last_appid}}; pagination loops while have_more_results is true, passing response.last_appid.
findings.details: Confirmed by Go clients Jleagle/steam-go (json tags appid, name, last_modified, price_change_number, have_more_results, last_appid) and gofurry/steam-go v1.3.12 (2026-09-26), and by jsnli/steamappidlist's daily job that loops on response.have_more_results / response.last_appid. Real rows from its 2026-10-27 dump: {appid:730,name:'Counter-Strike 2',last_modified:1793054556,price_change_number:39840616}; {appid:5495700,name:'Too Many Chickens',last_modified:1793069391,price_change_number:0}. A GitHub issue's 'app_id/last_app_id' naming is admittedly unverified and contradicted by working code.

findings.claim: A regular user Web API key works for IStoreService/GetAppList on api.steampowered.com; partner.steam-api.com must not be used without a publisher key.
findings.details: jsnli/steamappidlist calls https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?key=${STEAM_KEY}&include_games=...&max_results=50000 from GitHub Actions; its 2026-10-27 04:15Z commit holds rows with last_modified up to 04:14Z, so the call succeeds daily. Web API Overview: on the partner host 'Every request ... must be made with your publisher Web API key'; others get 403, and 403s 'will incur strict rate limits for the connecting IP'. A Jan-2026 report of 403 'with a key' (SteamAutoCracker #107) may be wrong host or limited account (unverified). Keyless: 403 'Access is denied. Retrying will not help.' (ground truth).

findings.claim: A full games pull with a key is 196,595 rows (~19.9 MB JSON), i.e. 4 calls at max_results=50000; DLC adds 63,919 rows (2 calls).
findings.details: Analysis of jsnli's 2026-10-27 dump (real GetAppList output, one category flag per run): games 196,595 rows, 19.92 MB (~101 B/row, ~5 MB per 50k page); DLC 63,919 (8.15 MB); software 2,917; videos 54; hardware 17. Appids strictly ascending, 0 duplicates, max appid 5,503,430; 18 games have an empty name. Keyless Query (US) reported 196,617 games the same week, so both cover released + coming-soon store pages.

findings.claim: GetAppList includes coming-soon, free and adult-only games and region-locked SKUs, but excludes delisted (unlisted) games.
findings.details: Checked 2026-10-27 dump vs live GetItems/Query: INCLUDED coming-soon pages (5495700 dated 2026-11; 1640150 TBA 'Por confirmarse'), free 570/730, adult-only games (20/20 sampled via Query content_descriptors_must_match [3]). EXCLUDED delisted games that GetItems flags unlisted:true: 50300 Spec Ops: The Line, 1293830 Forza Horizon 4, 241560 The Crew, 271590 GTA V Legacy. Region-agnostic: 5 of 1,005 appids <= 70300 (e.g. 22490 'Fallout: New Vegas' regional SKU, Championship Manager 2007/2008/2010) are in GetAppList but absent from Query with country_code US -> duplicate-looking names. Hidden pre-store apps: not listed (inference).

findings.claim: if_modified_since returns apps whose last_modified (any info or price change) is newer than the timestamp; ~3.3k games change per day, and deletions are never reported in deltas.
findings.details: Docs: last_modified 'indicates the last time some change was made to that game's information or price (not all of these changes may be visible on the store)'; if_modified_since filters to games 'changed or added since'; a changed price_change_number means the price may have changed. Observed: price_change_number is a global sequence shared by many apps (39626153 on 39,613 games; 0 on 58,371, likely never-priced pages) -> compare per app only. CS2 last_modified 1793054556 equals the ?t= in its asset_url_format, so asset/page edits bump it. Churn: 3,349 games in 24 h, 15,713 in 7 d, 35,504 in 30 d. Deletions absent from deltas (inference).

findings.claim: GetAppList returns a single non-localized base name per app, while GetItems/Query return names localized by context.language.
findings.details: GetAppList has no language parameter (e.g. 'ELDEN RING', 'Counter-Strike 2'); 13,361 game names contain characters outside Latin ranges (CJK, Cyrillic, symbols = developer base names). have_description_language=spanish could tag apps with a Spanish store description (~4 extra calls). Live GetItems with context.language='schinese' returned 艾尔登法环 (1245620), 黑神话：悟空 (2358720), 巫师3：狂猎 — 重制版 (292030). For a Spanish UI, index the base name plus the 'spanish' localized name as an alias (usually identical).

findings.claim: A key is registered at steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey and requires a non-limited account (at least US$5.00 spent) plus a Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator confirmation.
findings.details: Form asks for a domain name (node-steamcommunity docs: required string, 'localhost' acceptable) and ToU acceptance. Valve FAQ: limited accounts (< US$5.00 total store spend; gifted games do not count) lose 'Accessing the Steam Web API'. Key creation needs a mobile confirmation; without an authenticator: error NoMobileDevice (node-steamcommunity wiki); users noticed the confirmation by Jan 2024. One key per account (2013 forum answer); revoke/re-register any time. xPaw docs say the key may be sent as header x-webapi-key instead of ?key= (not live-tested).

findings.topic: Terms of Use limits and single key
findings.claim: The Steam Web API ToU caps usage at 100,000 calls per day, requires the key to stay confidential, and licenses it as personal and specific to your Application, so one server-side key per app is the right model.
findings.details: Quotes: 'You are limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day'; keep the key 'confidential, and not to share it with any third party'; license 'is personal to you and specific to your Application'; no use that 'degrades the operation or performance of Steam'; store Steam Data 'in a country (or countries) identified in your privacy policy'; Valve may terminate 'at any time'. ToU never asks for per-end-user keys (interpretation). Embedding the key in a web/mobile/desktop client would breach confidentiality. Catalog sync needs ~45 calls/day (<0.05% of the cap).

findings.claim: Valve publishes no per-second or per-IP limits; community measurements put Steam at roughly 120 requests per 5-minute window per IP.
findings.details: mparmol/Removed_Steam_Games (2026): 'Measured: ~120 requests per ~5 min window, per IP, regardless of how fast they are sent' (endpoint unspecified). SteamDB blog: store appdetails limited to ~200 requests/5 min since July 2015. Forum reports of multi-hour 429 bans. Official: 403s on the partner host trigger strict IP limits. Responses carry header X-eresult (1 = OK; SteamKit EResult 84 = RateLimitExceeded, 15 = AccessDenied). Shared serverless egress IPs may share these budgets (inference). This research's ~20 spaced requests saw no 429.

findings.claim: IStoreQueryService/Query/v1 works without a key today and can enumerate all ~196.6k games at 1000 ids per call, using sort=2 for stable ascending-appid paging.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28, no key: input_json {query:{start,count,sort,filters:{type_filters:{include_games:true}}},context:{language,country_code}} -> 200. count capped at 1000 (asked 5000 -> metadata.count 1000); start=195000 returned 1000 ids; sort=2 strictly ascending (999/999); default sort 0 not monotonic (8 breaks in 1000). total_matching_records moved 196,607 -> 196,617 in ~10 min (live index: offset paging can drift). ids-only page 18 KB/0.3 s; with data_request include_release 756 KB/1.2 s. Undocumented (xPaw marks it undocumented and lists key as required; mparmol also reports keyless) -> may change.

findings.claim: Query exposes released_only, coming_soon_only, per-type filters, tag/price/date/content-descriptor/review filters and data_request flags; sort 2 = ascending appid.
findings.details: query{start,count,sort,filters{released_only,coming_soon_only,type_filters{include_apps,_packages,_bundles,_games,_demos,_mods,_dlc,_software,_video,_hardware,_series,_music,dlc_for_appid},tagids_must_match,tagids_exclude,price_filters,release_date_filter,content_descriptors_must_match/_excluded,review_score_filter,global_top_n_sellers,parent_appids}}, context{language,elanguage,country_code}, data_request{include_basic_info,include_release,include_assets,include_platforms,include_reviews,include_tag_count,include_supported_languages...}. Sort ids (community doc): 1 alphabetical, 2 appid asc (verified live), 20 most recent, 21 % positive reviews. Default count 10.

findings.claim: On 2026-10-28 the Steam store index holds 317,807 apps, including 196,617 games (133,880 released + 62,681 coming soon), 63,079 DLC, 43,376 demos, 11,595 soundtracks and 2,919 software titles.
findings.details: Keyless Query, country_code US, count=0: include_apps 317,807; include_games 196,617 = released_only 133,880 + coming_soon_only 62,681 (~32% of 'games' are unreleased pages); DLC 63,079; demos 43,376; music 11,595; software 2,919; games with content descriptor 3 (adult-only sexual content) 9,674. Store search (category1=998 Games, cc=ES) reports 186,626, roughly the Query total minus adult-only titles (inference: anonymous search hides them). Sizing: ~197k games (or ~134k released) is small enough to index entirely.

findings.claim: SteamDB counts 21,268 games released in 2025 and 20,220 in 2026 through October 1.
findings.details: TheGamer (2026-10-02, citing SteamDB): 21,268 releases in 2025; 20,220 in 2026 up to Oct 1 (projected ~21,376 by end of Oct). tech-insider (2026-09-29): 'Steam's storefront listed 135,003 games as of July 18, 2026' (source unnamed). SteamDB homepage reportedly shows ~570k apps and 1.89M packages in its DB (includes configs, betas, tools, unreleased; not verified, steamdb.info returns 403 to fetchers). 2024 analysis of the old full list: 204,038 IDs on 2024-06-23, ~160 IDs added and ~20 removed per day.

findings.claim: Keyless IStoreBrowseService/GetItems returns, per appid, the signals needed to classify games: type, visibility, localized name, coming-soon/early-access/release info, content descriptors and unlisted.
findings.details: Fields: success (EResult, 1 OK), visible, name (localized), store_url_path, type (EStoreAppType 0 game, 1 demo, 2 mod, 3 movie, 4 DLC, 6 software, 7 video, 8 series, 10 hardware, 11 music, 12 beta, 13 tool), is_free, is_early_access, is_coming_soon, release{steam_release_date, coming_soon_display 'date_full'/'text_tba', custom_release_date_message}, content_descriptorids, unlisted (proto field 55), unvailable_for_country_restriction (field 5, sic), best_purchase_option, assets. Invalid appid 1 -> success 15 (AccessDenied), visible false, name ''. Batch ~200 ids/call (URL-length bound; community).

findings.claim: Delisted games are detectable only via GetItems unlisted:true (they still return a name); appdetails still answers success:true for them, and neither GetAppList nor Query lists them.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: GetItems returned success 1, visible true, name and unlisted:true (no best_purchase_option) for 50300, 1293830, 241560, 271590; purchasable 19000 has best_purchase_option and no unlisted. store/api/appdetails?appids=50300 returns success:true with full data, so it cannot detect delisting. mparmol/Removed_Steam_Games: 4 of 7 'removal' candidates were region blocks, so they declare removal only if invisible in ES, US, JP and CN. Consequence: a first sync today cannot discover games delisted earlier; support lookup by appid/store URL.

findings.claim: Store web search endpoints are keyless but unsuitable as a catalog backbone; they work only as live typeahead fallbacks.
findings.details: search/results/?query&start=0&count=200&category1=998&infinite=1&cc=ES -> JSON {success,results_html,total_count:186626,start} with only 100 HTML rows (cap), i.e. ~1,870 scraped calls for the catalog. api/storesearch/?term=elden%20ring&l=spanish&cc=ES -> {total:6,items[{type,name,id,price,tiny_image,metascore,platforms,controller_support}]}, max 10 items, no CORS (community). IStoreQueryService/SearchSuggestions (keyless; search_term, max_results, filters, data_request) returned 367520 and 1030300 for 'hollow kni' in 0.29 s.

findings.claim: api.steampowered.com sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so browsers cannot call Steam directly and ingestion must run server-side.
findings.details: A Query request sent with 'Origin: https://example.com' got no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (only X-eresult: 1; responses use Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store). yukimajik/steam-review-sentiment PR #3 (2026-10-07): storesearch 'sends no CORS header, so browsers can't read it directly'. With the ToU key-confidentiality rule, all Steam calls belong in a scheduled job, serverless function or local Node backend; the app reads from its own DB/snapshot.

findings.claim: SteamSpy request=all returns 1,000 owner-sorted games per page, is limited to 1 request per 60 s and refreshes daily, so it is only a popularity signal, not a catalog.
findings.details: steamspy.com/api.php: 'Returns 1,000 entries per page', pages start at 0; 'Allowed poll rate - 1 request per second for most requests, 1 request per 60 seconds for the *all* requests'; 'data is refreshed once a day'. Live page 0: 1,000 entries, 355 KB, Cache-Control max-age=86400; fields appid, name, developer, publisher, positive, negative, owners ('10,000,000 .. 20,000,000'), ccu, price, initialprice, discount. Only games with owner estimates (no coming-soon pages); no stated license.

findings.claim: PICS through node-steam-user anonymous logon exposes every app including unreleased and delisted ones, but needs a persistent CM connection and frequent polling of a short changenumber window.
findings.details: steam-user 5.3.0 (npm metadata 2025-12-04): logOn({anonymous:true}); getProductChanges(since) -> currentChangenumber + appChanges[{appid,change_number,needs_token}]; >~5,000 changenumbers back returns only the current number (README; mparmol measured ~7,200, ~9.5 h). getProductInfo(apps,packages,inclTokens) -> appinfo (common.type/name/releasestate). EAppType (SteamKit): Game 1, Application 2, Tool 4, Demo 8, DLC 32, Config 256, Hardware 512, Video 2048, Music 8192, Beta 65536; EAppReleaseState: Unavailable 1, Prerelease 2, PreloadOnly 3, Released 4, Disabled 5. No browser use; not covered by Web API ToU (gray area).

findings.claim: SteamDB offers no public API and forbids scraping, so it cannot be a data source.
findings.details: SteamDB FAQ: 'Does SteamDB have an API?' -> 'In short, no'; scraping/crawling 'is not allowed' and may get you automatically banned; no data dumps except academic requests; no publishing the data in its entirety or AI training. It points developers to Steam's WebAPI/SteamKit. steamdb.info returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches during this research.

findings.claim: The games list contains junk and noise that name-prefix filters handle badly: empty names, placeholder titles, years-old TBA pages and adult-only titles.
findings.details: In 196,595 games: 18 empty names; placeholders 'TestApp' (866490), 'UNTITLED' (639770), 'Untitled' (1025620), but prefix filters would drop 'Untitled Goose Game' (837470) or 'Test Drive: Ferrari Racing Legends' (211970). 71 names contain 'Demo', 4 'Soundtrack', 3 'Playtest' despite type game. 62,681 coming-soon pages, many TBA for years (1640150 TBA, last_modified 2024-03). Adult: content_descriptorids (live: appid 10 -> [2,5]; HuniePop -> [1,3,4,5]); id 5 = General Mature Content (2024 analysis); 3 = adult-only sexual content (label from memory, consistent with samples).

findings.claim: A keyed backbone plus keyless enrichment needs only ~45 Steam calls per day after a bootstrap of about 4 GetAppList calls plus a ~197-call Query pass.
findings.details: Bootstrap: 4 GetAppList calls (~20 MB, <1 min) + keyless Query sort=2 pass with include_release for flags (197 calls, ~150 MB, ~8 min at ~120 req/5 min) instead of ~983 GetItems calls. Steady state: hourly delta if_modified_since=lastStart-3600 (~140 rows avg, 24 calls/day); GetItems for changed ids (3,349/day / 200 = ~17 calls); weekly full reconcile (4 calls) + GetItems on missing ids (1-5 calls). ~45 calls/day = 0.045% of the 100k ToU cap. Keyless fallback: daily full Query pass (197 calls) + hourly tail check of the highest appids.

findings.claim: A names-only index of all ~196.6k Steam games is about 1.9 MB brotli (2.6 MB gzip), small enough to ship to clients for instant offline search.
findings.details: From the 2026-10-27 dump: 196,577 named games -> appid+name TSV 5.19 MB, gzip -9 2.56 MB, brotli 1.89 MB; JSON [[appid,name],...] 5.98 MB / 2.64 MB gzip / 1.91 MB brotli. Median name 14 chars, p99 50, max 414. One full download + small daily deltas (~3k changed rows/day) allows instant local search (e.g. IndexedDB + in-memory prefix/fuzzy index), with server-side SearchSuggestions only for misses.

recommendations: Make keyed IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 on https://api.steampowered.com (never partner.steam-api.com) the catalog backbone, called only by a server-side scheduled job with ONE Web API key kept in secrets; MVP: include_games=true only, add include_dlc=true later if users want to note expansions.

Bootstrap: loop max_results=50000 with last_appid until have_more_results is false (~4 calls); checkpoint the cursor after each page; upsert by appid (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(appid) DO UPDATE ... only when name/last_modified/price_change_number changed) and stamp last_seen_run.

Incremental: every 1-6 h call with if_modified_since = start of the last successful run minus 3600 s (overlap absorbed by idempotent upserts) and page on have_more_results; expect ~3.3k changed games/day and occasional bulk bursts.

Removal detection: weekly full pass; ids not seen -> batch GetItems (<=200 ids, contexts ES and US): unlisted:true -> status 'delisted' (keep searchable with a badge); success != 1 or invisible in all contexts -> 'gone' (hide from search). Soft-delete only; never drop rows referenced by any user list.

Enrichment: for new/changed appids call keyless IStoreBrowseService/GetItems with context {language:'spanish', country_code:'ES'} and data_request {include_release, include_assets, include_basic_info as needed} to store type, is_coming_soon, release date/coming_soon_display, is_early_access, is_free, content_descriptorids, localized name and capsule assets; for the initial bulk use one keyless Query sort=2 pass (197 calls).

HTTP policy: one worker, <=0.4 req/s per IP; check HTTP status and the X-eresult header; 429 -> exponential backoff with jitter 60 s to 15 min (honor Retry-After if present), abort after ~5 consecutive 429s and resume from the saved cursor next schedule; 5xx/timeouts -> up to 5 retries (2,4,8,16,32 s); 403 on keyed calls -> stop and alert (revoked key or limited account).
Keep a feature-flagged keyless fallback: enumerate with IStoreQueryService/Query sort=2, count=1000, start += 950 (50-item overlap), dedupe by appid and reconcile against total_matching_records.

For 'rapida y agil' search, publish a compact snapshot of [appid, name, localized alias, flags] (~1.9 MB brotli for all games) plus daily deltas so clients search locally and offline; use server-side SearchSuggestions only for misses.

Support adding by Steam store URL or appid (GetItems lookup) to cover delisted or region-locked games missing from the catalog, plus fully custom entries for non-Steam platforms (PlayStation 'platinado').

Ranking/filters: boost released and popular titles (Query include_reviews or SteamSpy owners at 1 req/60 s), demote TBA coming-soon pages, hide adult-only (descriptor 3) behind a setting, drop empty names and use an exact-match placeholder blacklist instead of prefix filters; de-duplicate regional SKUs with identical names.

Do not use ISteamApps/GetAppList (gone), SteamDB (no API, scraping forbidden) or appdetails for bulk ingestion (~200 req/5 min, no delisting signal); postpone PICS unless completeness for deleted/unreleased apps becomes a requirement.
Publish a privacy policy naming the country where Steam Data is stored and keep the Valve attribution allowed by the ToU.
risks: Undocumented keyless endpoints (IStoreQueryService/Query, IStoreBrowseService/GetItems, SearchSuggestions) can start requiring a key or change shape without notice; ISteamApps/GetAppList itself vanished with no dated announcement.

The key is tied to a personal Steam account: if the account becomes limited (< US$5 spend), loses its mobile authenticator, or Valve terminates the license ('at any time'), the backbone stops; keep the keyless fallback and alerting.
Per-IP throttling (~120 req/5 min community-measured, multi-hour 429 bans reported); shared serverless/CI IPs may be throttled because of other tenants.

Delisted games are absent from both GetAppList and Query; games delisted before the first sync cannot be discovered without PICS or third-party dumps, so users won't find them unless appid/URL lookup exists.

Search noise: ~62.7k coming-soon pages (many TBA for years), ~9.7k adult-only games, placeholder apps and regional duplicate SKUs (e.g. two 'Fallout: New Vegas') degrade results unless ranked and filtered.
Region effects: Query/GetItems results depend on context.country_code; a US-only context hides some regional SKUs, an ES context may hide others.
Offset paging on the live Query index can skip or duplicate items when apps are added or removed mid-pass; needs overlap and reconciliation.
Deltas never report deletions; without a periodic full reconcile, delisted games keep looking available.
open_questions: Is if_modified_since inclusive or exclusive, and does a coming-soon -> released transition always bump last_modified? (needs a keyed test)
Does GetAppList coverage depend on the key owner's country? Evidence (regional SKUs present) suggests region-agnostic, untested with a key.
Exact per-IP limits for api.steampowered.com Query/GetItems, and whether 429 responses carry Retry-After.
Maximum ids per GetItems call (community ~200, URL-length bound) and whether input_protobuf_encoded/POST lifts it.
Official label mapping of content_descriptorids 1-5 (3 strongly implies adult-only sexual content).
Is anonymous PICS use acceptable to Valve for a public app? No explicit policy found.
Should DLC/expansions (~64k) be in scope for 'juegos que quieres jugar'? Costs 2 extra calls per full sync plus UI work.
Which non-Steam catalogs (PlayStation for 'platinado', others) will follow? That is a separate data-source dimension.

researches.label: metadata & media
researches.summary:
The best single source for enrichment is the keyless IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1, live-tested on 2026-10-28 with 23 polite requests. Batch size is limited by URL length (about 8 KB), not by a fixed count: 250 seven-digit appids per JSON GET, and 800 passed with input_protobuf_encoded, which returns binary protobuf. context.country_code is mandatory; without it the call returns an empty {response:{}}. context.language localizes text: CJK names, descriptions, review labels and release messages.

One batched call can return, per game:
- localized name and type (EStoreAppType)
- release: Unix timestamps plus is_coming_soon and coming_soon_display (date_full, text_comingsoon or text_tba) with a localized message
- platforms and Steam Deck category
- developers, publishers and short description (basic_info)
- weighted tags (include_tag_count)
- review summary (include_reviews)
- achievement_count, genreids and metacritic (include_extra_details, heavy at 0.4-7 KB per item)
- content descriptors (returned by default)
- asset filenames

Delisted games still come back with success 1 and unlisted:true. Removed or nonexistent ids return success 15 with appid 0, so key results by id. include_best_purchase_option defaults to true; turn it off.

Images: the URL is https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/ + asset_url_format, with ${FILENAME} replaced by the filename. This matches appdetails header_image exactly. Filenames vary (library_600x900.jpg, <sha1>/library_capsule.jpg, portrait.png, none for DLC). Never guess legacy names: they return 404 for new games and stale art for old ones. Use library_capsule as the vertical cover and header as the fallback (present for all 176 sample items). CDN images send ACAO * and a max-age of about 10 years.

CORS: the Steam API and store endpoints send no ACAO, even with an origin= param. A PWA therefore needs a proxy or a static snapshot; Tauri (Rust http plugin) or a server can call Steam directly. API cache hints are short: GetItems 120 s, appdetails 3600 s, tag and category lists no-store.

appdetails takes one appid per call (several only with filters=price_overview, otherwise 400 with body null). It is heavy (42 KB raw), returns localized date strings ('3 AGO 2023'), and has a historic limit of about 200 requests per 5 minutes, so use it only on demand. /appreviews was retired on 2026-10-22 (live: 302); use the GetItems summary, or IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews for review text. GetTagList (446 Spanish tags, version_hash) and GetStoreCategories (72) are keyless. There is no endpoint for genre names.

Strategy has two tiers:
1. A server or cron job builds a compact snapshot per game: appid, name, year, type, coming-soon flag, cover, t, popularity. That is about 19-48 B per game gzipped, or 3-7 MB for 150k games, for instant local search. It costs about 600 JSON or 215 protobuf calls.
2. When the user adds a game, fetch full flags for that game only (3-10 KB) and refresh it periodically.

findings.claim: IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1 is keyless and takes input_json {ids:[StoreItemID], context:StoreBrowseContext, data_request:StoreBrowseItemDataRequest} via GET.
findings.details: StoreItemID: appid|packageid|bundleid|tagid|creatorid|hubcategoryid|salepagegid. context: language (Steam API code: spanish, latam, english, schinese), elanguage, country_code, steam_realm (optional; community enum 1=Global, 2=China). data_request has 20 fields: include_assets, include_release, include_platforms, include_all_purchase_options, include_screenshots, include_trailers, include_ratings, include_tag_count (int N), include_reviews, include_basic_info, include_supported_languages, include_full_description, include_included_items, included_item_data_request (nested), include_assets_without_overrides, apply_user_filters, include_links, include_extra_details, include_best_purchase_option (default TRUE), include_optin_registration_tags. Proto updated 2026-10-22.

findings.claim: GetItems returns HTTP 200 with an empty {"response":{}} when context.country_code is omitted; with country_code it returns store_items.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: context {language:'spanish'} only gave a 35-byte {response:{}}. The same ids with country_code 'ES' returned full items. Community (ludarium PR #60, Sep 2026) reports the same. language drives localized text: Spanish short_description, review_score_label ('Muy positivas'), custom_release_date_message ('Proximamente'/'Por confirmarse'). country_code drives prices (EUR, '59,99€') and the game_rating agency (ES gives PEGI). steam_realm can be omitted (works without it).

findings.claim: GetItems batch size is bounded by URL length (~8 KB), not a fixed count: 250 seven-digit appids via JSON GET and 800 appids via input_protobuf_encoded both succeeded live.
findings.details: Live JSON: input_json for 250 ids = 7,720 URL-encoded chars gave HTTP 200 with 250 items (210 KB raw / 37 KB gzip, 0.63 s). Community (ludarium PR #60, 2026-09-17): 300 ids gives 400, POST gives 405, so they cap at 200. Live protobuf: the same request as base64 protobuf in input_protobuf_encoded with 800 ids (6,538-char param) gave HTTP 200 with all 800 items, Content-Type application/octet-stream (binary protobuf, 240 KB raw / 83 KB gzip, 1.0 s). Appids >= 2,097,152 need 4-byte varints (~7 B/id), so ~700 ids per protobuf call is the safe ceiling. A count cap above 800 is untested.

findings.topic: GetItems default fields and flag outputs
findings.claim: With no flags, GetItems returns id, success, visible, name, store_url_path, appid, type, categories and content_descriptorids, plus a price object, because include_best_purchase_option defaults to true.
findings.details: Default extras when applicable: is_free, is_early_access, is_coming_soon, unlisted, related_items.parent_appid (DLC or soundtrack to its base game). Flag to field: assets, release, platforms, reviews, basic_info {short_description, publishers[], developers[], franchises[]}, tag_count:N gives tagids[] + tags[{tagid,weight}], ratings gives game_rating, extra_details, full_description gives full_description_bbcode (BBCode, not HTML), screenshots, trailers, supported_languages (elanguage ints), links, all_purchase_options. Measured raw size per item: extra_details 0.36-6.8 KB, trailers up to 5.9 KB, full description up to 8.4 KB, assets ~1 KB, tags 0.56 KB, reviews 0.25 KB.

findings.claim: GetItems numeric fields map to protobuf enums: type=EStoreAppType (0 Game, 1 Demo, 4 DLC, 6 Software, 11 Music, 12 Beta/playtest), success=EResult (1 OK, 15 AccessDenied), review_score 0-9, steam_deck_compat_category 0-3.
findings.details: item_type: 0 App, 1 Package, 2 Bundle, 3 Mtx, 4 Tag, 5 Creator, 6 HubCategory, 7 SalePage. EStoreAppType: 0 Game, 1 Demo, 2 Mod, 3 Movie, 4 DLC, 5 Guide, 6 Software, 7 Video, 8 Series, 9 Episode, 10 Hardware, 11 Music, 12 Beta, 13 Tool, 14 Advertising. EUserReviewScore: 0 None, 1 OverwhelminglyNeg, 2 VeryNeg, 3 Neg, 4 MostlyNeg, 5 Mixed, 6 MostlyPos, 7 Positive, 8 VeryPos, 9 OverwhelminglyPos. Deck: 0 Unknown, 1 Unsupported, 2 Playable, 3 Verified (steam_os/frame/machine fields likely share it; inference). Live run of 800 consecutive ids: 251 success 15; of the rest, 381 game, 42 demo, 93 DLC, 3 software, 23 music, 7 beta.

findings.claim: Delisted games still return success 1 with full data and unlisted:true; nonexistent or removed ids return success 15, visible false, appid 0 and an empty name.
findings.details: Live: Forza Horizon 4 (1293830), The Crew (241560) and Spec Ops: The Line (50300) gave success 1, visible true, unlisted true, names, assets and reviews, but no purchase_options or best_purchase_option. The Crew also carries purchase_notes with a localized delisting and server-shutdown note. appid 999999999 gave success 15 and store_url_path 'app/0/'. Community (ludarium, Sep 2026): the removed game Firefall also returns 15 with appid 0. Always key results by the 'id' field. Keep unlisted games searchable (users own them) but flag them.

findings.claim: release gives Unix-second timestamps plus coming-soon display metadata; TBA and 'coming soon' titles have no timestamp, only a localized message.
findings.details: Seen: steam_release_date, original_release_date (sometimes 0), original_steam_release_date (relaunches), is_coming_soon, coming_soon_display, custom_release_date_message, is_early_access. Live: Project Android 3690240 {1793149200 = 2026-10-28T01:00Z, date_full}; Guild of Souls {text_comingsoon, 'Proximamente'}; Deadlock {text_tba, 'Por confirmarse'}; CS2 1345568400 (2012-08-21, CS:GO's date). Steamworks docs list 5 display formats (exact date, month, quarter, year, Coming Soon); vague dates are listed at the last possible date of their range and the exact date is hidden. Month/quarter/year values were not observed; names like date_month are unverified.

findings.topic: Image URL construction and CDN hosts
findings.claim: The final image URL is 'https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/' + assets.asset_url_format, with the literal '${FILENAME}' replaced by the asset filename.
findings.details: Live: format 'steam/apps/1086940/${FILENAME}?t=1777363040' + header '48a2fcbd.../header.jpg' reproduces exactly the appdetails header_image .../store_item_assets/steam/apps/1086940/48a2fcbda8565bb45025e98fd8ebde8a7203f6a0/header.jpg?t=1777363040. t = assets.last_modified. Screenshot filenames are full relative paths ('steam/apps/<id>/ss_<sha1>.jpg?t=') on the same base. Hosts on 2026-10-28: shared.akamai and shared.fastly gave 200; shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com gave 301 to shared.steamstatic.com (not fetched). Legacy cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/ and steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steam/apps/ still give 200 for old files.

findings.claim: Guessed hash-less legacy filenames are unreliable: they return 404 for new games and can serve outdated art for older ones.
findings.details: Live HEAD: Guild of Souls 5338720 (hashed assets only): /store_item_assets/steam/apps/5338720/library_600x900.jpg 404 and /header.jpg 404. CS2: hash-less header.jpg gave 200 but Last-Modified 2023-09-18 (34,296 B), while the API's hashed header is Last-Modified 2026-06-02 (33,545 B, different ETag), so it is stale. Deadlock: hash-less library_600x900.jpg returns an Aug-2024 file, while the API lists '43ca731f.../library_capsule.jpg'. Community projects hit the same issue in 2026 and switched to GetItems asset paths.

findings.claim: assets.library_capsule (600x900 portrait) is the right cover, but its filename varies and most DLC lack it; assets.header was present for every valid item and is the safest fallback.
findings.details: In 176 valid sample items, library_capsule was 'library_600x900.jpg' 133 times, '<sha1>/library_capsule.jpg' 3 (newest games), absent 30 (all DLC) and 'portrait.png' 10 (soundtracks). Also seen: '<sha1>/library_600x900.jpg' (3690240), and 'portrait.png' for the game The Crew (a 545 KB PNG). header present 176/176. Sizes: CS2 header 33.5 KB, library 38 KB; Spec Ops library 67.7 KB. Steamworks: Library Capsule 600x900 is required. Fallback chain: library_capsule, then header or main_capsule (letterboxed), then a generated placeholder. Use _2x only for hi-DPI detail views.

findings.claim: Steam CDN images send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and very long cache lifetimes, so clients can cache covers indefinitely.
findings.details: Live HEAD with Origin https://example.com: every 200 image response had ACAO '*'. store_item_assets on shared.akamai: Cache-Control public, max-age~315,269,382 (~10 years), ETag and Last-Modified. shared.fastly: max-age=315360000 plus X-Cache. Legacy cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com: max-age=113408 (~31 h). steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net: max-age=604800 (7 days). Paths are content-hashed and carry ?t=last_modified, so new art means a new URL. A PWA can keep covers in Cache Storage as non-opaque responses and draw them on canvas without tainting.

findings.claim: api.steampowered.com and store.steampowered.com send no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to third-party origins, so a browser or PWA cannot read GetItems or appdetails responses directly.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28 with Origin: https://example.com: GetItems, GetTagList, GetStoreCategories, appdetails and featuredcategories all returned no ACAO header. Adding the query param origin=https://example.com to GetItems also returned none. Consequences: a PWA needs its own proxy or edge function, or a prebuilt static snapshot served with CORS. Tauri can call Steam from Rust via tauri-plugin-http (reqwest, URL allow-list in capabilities), where browser CORS does not apply (inference). A server or cron job has no CORS limit but puts all traffic on one IP for rate limiting.

findings.claim: Steam API cache hints are short and come without ETags: GetItems max-age=120, appdetails max-age=3600, featuredcategories max-age=300, and GetTagList/GetStoreCategories no-store.
findings.details: Live headers: GetItems 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=120' ('private, max-age=120' on the all-flags request), X-eresult: 1, gzip, no ETag or Last-Modified, so conditional GETs are impossible. appdetails (including filters=price_overview) 'public,max-age=3600', Expires +1 h, Last-Modified on the hour. featuredcategories 'public,max-age=300'. IStoreService/GetTagList and IStoreBrowseService/GetStoreCategories 'max-age=0, no-cache, no-store', but GetTagList offers version_hash/have_version_hash. Implement your own TTL cache.

findings.claim: store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails accepts several appids only with filters=price_overview; any other multi-appid request returns HTTP 400 with body 'null'.
findings.details: Live: appids=5338720,3690240&filters=release_date,genres gave 400 'null'. appids=1086940,1245620,730,1293830&filters=price_overview&cc=es gave 200; free (730) and delisted (1293830) games came back as "data": [] (an array, not an object). A full single call (BG3, l=spanish) is 41.7 KB raw / 8.5 KB gzip with: genres [{id:'25',description:'Aventura'}...], 27 localized categories, achievements {total:54, highlighted[]}, metacritic, recommendations.total, release_date {coming_soon:false, date:'3 AGO 2023'} (localized, hard to parse) and header_image; no vertical capsule. Historic limit ~200 req/5 min per IP (SteamDB 2015, community ~2024; unverified for 2026).

findings.topic: Achievements, genres and metacritic via extra_details
findings.claim: GetItems include_extra_details returns batched, keyless achievement_count, genreids and metacritic score, matching appdetails.
findings.details: Fields: extra_details.links_and_info {genreids[], achievements_visible, achievement_count, website}, extra_details.metacritic {score, url}, steam_award[]. Live: CS2 1 achievement, genreids [37,1]. BG3 54 (= appdetails achievements.total 54), [3,25,2], metacritic 96. ELDEN RING 42; Forza Horizon 4 178; Spec Ops 50; unreleased Deadlock none. Cost: 0.36-6.8 KB raw per item, because it also carries system requirements, legal text and EULAs. Cheaper boolean signal: default categories include feature id 22 'Logros de Steam'. These are Steam achievements only, not PlayStation trophies.

findings.claim: IStoreService/GetTagList/v1 is keyless and returns every store tag localized (446 Spanish tags on 2026-10-28) with a version_hash.
findings.details: Live: input_json={language:'spanish'} returned 446 tags, version_hash '569874580', ~16.7 KB raw / 5 KB gzip. Examples: 19 'Accion', 122 'Rol', 21 'Aventura', 9 'Estrategia', 1663 'FPS', 4182 'Un jugador'. The request accepts have_version_hash (proto) for change detection. Per-game tags come from GetItems include_tag_count:N as tagids[] (ordered) and tags[{tagid,weight}] (BG3 top tag 122, weight 954); tagids are absent without that flag. IStoreService/GetLocalizedNameForTags (language + tagids[] to english_name, name, normalized_name) has the same keyless annotation but was not tested.

findings.claim: IStoreBrowseService/GetStoreCategories/v1 is keyless and returns 72 localized categories; no endpoint was found that names the numeric genre ids.
findings.details: Live (spanish): 72 categories with categoryid, type (EStoreCategoryType: 0 Category x5, 1 SupportedPlayers x13, 2 Feature x46, 3 ControllerSupport x8, 4 CloudGaming), internal_name, display_name and computed. Examples: 2 'Un jugador', 1 'Multijugador', 9 'Cooperativo', 22 'Logros de Steam', 28 'Compat. total con mando', 62 'Prestamo familiar'. These match the GetItems categories.supported_player/feature/controller id lists. Genre names are only available from appdetails genres (string id + localized description), e.g. 25 Aventura, 3 Rol, 2 Estrategia. Build a small static table per language; the community also found no official list.

findings.claim: Keyless GetItems returns adult-only games, so filtering must happen client-side on content_descriptorids (EContentDescriptorID 1-5), which is returned by default.
findings.details: Enum: 1 NudityOrSexualContent, 2 FrequentViolenceOrGore, 3 AdultOnlySexualContent, 4 GratuitousSexualContent, 5 AnyMatureContent. Live sample: 37 of 176 valid items had descriptors, including 7 with 3 and 7 with 4 (~4%). CS2 [2,5], BG3 [1,2,5]. Hide ids 3/4 (names included) by default behind an opt-in toggle. include_ratings adds the country-specific game_rating (ES: PEGI 18, required_age 18, use_age_gate). IStoreQueryService also has a content_descriptors_excluded filter.

findings.claim: Use GetItems include_reviews for batched review summaries; store.steampowered.com/appreviews/<appid>?json=1 is retired (302 to the store home) and replaced by IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1.
findings.details: GetItems returns reviews.summary_filtered (+ summary_language_specific) {review_count, percent_positive, review_score 0-9, localized review_score_label}; BG3: 760,008 reviews, 96%, score 9. Live: /appreviews/1086940?json=1 gave 302 to https://store.steampowered.com/. Valve docs mark it deprecated; the community reports retirement on 2026-10-22. GetAppReviews: keyless, input_json, languages[], num_per_page max 100, totals only on page 1 with review_type 0, a shared lower anonymous limit (429), cached up to 10 min. Community caveats: GetItems counts Steam purchases only, and once showed 0 for a game with thousands of reviews.

findings.claim: The GetItems 'name' field follows context.language: Simplified Chinese returned localized titles, while Spanish returned the English titles for every tested game.
findings.details: Live with language 'schinese', country US: 2358720 Black Myth: Wukong, 1091500 Cyberpunk 2077, 1245620 ELDEN RING and 1086940 BG3 all came back with their Chinese titles, and store_url_slug was localized too. With 'spanish' the names stayed English ('ELDEN RING', "Baldur's Gate 3", 'Counter-Strike 2'). Build the search index from english names and add the user-language name only as an alias when it differs; for Spanish that costs almost nothing. Use 'latam' for Latin-American Spanish text.

findings.claim: Rate limits for keyless GetItems are undocumented; 6 GetItems calls (8 api.steampowered.com calls in total) over ~10 minutes today all returned 200, and community reports point to per-IP throttling.
findings.details: Observed latency was 0.6-1.0 s per call, with no 429. Valve publishes no number. Community (2026): keyless endpoints are throttled per IP. One report of ~1 request per 3 s before 429 could not be traced to a primary source. free-steam-games-list (2026-10-23) refreshes reviews daily in 50-id batches in about 2 minutes. The retired /appreviews was measured at ~270 burst, ~0.96 req/s refill and ~4.5 min block (Arkhemis, 2026-09-27). Plan for at most 1 request per second, one at a time, with exponential backoff and a global pause on 429.

findings.claim: Enriching about 150k games takes ~600 JSON GetItems calls (250 ids each) or ~215 protobuf calls (700 ids each), roughly 4-30 minutes at one call every 1-3 s.
findings.details: Snapshot flags {include_assets, include_release, include_reviews, include_best_purchase_option:false}: 250 ids is about 210 KB raw / 37 KB gzip per call (measured with prices on), ~22 MB gzip for 150k games. Full detail flags (basic_info, platforms, tag_count 20, extra_details) cost about 3-10 KB raw per game, so fetch those lazily: when a user adds or opens a game, make one call for it, or batch the user's list at up to 250 ids per call. appdetails at ~0.67 req/s would need ~62 h for 150k, so use it only on demand. The 150k figure is an assumption; take the real catalog size from R1.

findings.claim: A compact catalog row [appid, name, year, type] measures ~42 B raw JSON / ~19 B gzip; adding cover path + last_modified gives ~27 B gzip with legacy filenames and up to ~48 B gzip with 40-hex hashed paths.
findings.details: Measured on 176 real items: without cover 42.4 B raw, 18.6 B gzip, 14.8 B brotli. Adding [is_coming_soon, library_capsule filename, last_modified]: 74.5 raw, 26.5 gzip, 20.5 brotli. If every cover were '<sha1>/library_capsule.jpg': 108 raw, 47.9 gzip, 40.2 brotli (hex hashes do not compress). Average name 16.7 UTF-8 bytes (max 51). For 150k games: about 2.8, 4.0 or 7.2 MB gzip. To shrink: store the hash as 20 raw bytes, the filename as an enum code, and drop covers for non-games. A one-byte log-scaled review_count adds 1-2 B per row and greatly improves search ranking.

findings.claim: Suggested cadence: refresh coming-soon titles daily, games released in the last ~90 days weekly, everything else monthly, and the tag list weekly via version_hash.
findings.details: Why: coming-soon items flip state at release (Project Android was still date_full for 2026-10-28T01:00Z on its launch day), and their dates or display modes change. Review scores move fast in the first weeks. Assets change rarely (last_modified; Forza Horizon 4's assets changed 2024-12-16, right after delisting). Budget: if there are ~10-20k coming-soon items (unverified), a daily refresh is 40-80 JSON calls. Re-enrich any item whose cover returns 404. Treat success 15 as removed only after 2 consecutive misses.

findings.claim: IStoreQueryService/Query carries the same keyless annotation as GetItems and can list items by filter (coming_soon_only, released_only, type_filters, content_descriptors_excluded) with the same StoreItem data; it was not tested here.
findings.details: Proto: CStoreQuery_Query_Request {query_name, query: CStoreQueryParams {start, count (default 10), sort, filters}, context, data_request, override_country_code}. Response: {metadata {total_matching_records, start, count}, ids[], store_items[]}. Annotated 'bConstMethod=true, ePrivilege=1, eWebAPIKeyRequirement=1, rgBrowserAPISites', like GetItems. It would let a refresher fetch all coming-soon games without knowing their appids. Keyless access, the maximum count per page and the rate limit are unverified.

recommendations: Use IStoreBrowseService/GetItems as the only bulk enrichment source. Always send context.country_code (e.g. ES) and a language ('english' for the canonical search name, 'spanish' or 'latam' for display text). Key results by 'id' and skip success != 1.
Set include_best_purchase_option:false unless prices are shown. Request only include_assets + include_release + include_reviews for the catalog snapshot.
Batch up to 200-250 ids per JSON GET (stay under ~7.5 KB of URL). Optionally use input_protobuf_encoded with ~600-700 ids per call (needs the SteamTracking .proto files with protobufjs or prost).

Two-tier data model. (1) A server or cron job builds a compact catalog snapshot per game: appid, english name, alias, year, type, coming-soon flag, cover filename, t, popularity byte, unlisted flag, adult flag. That is about 3-7 MB gzip for ~150k games; the client downloads it once and searches locally for instant results. (2) When a game is added to the backlog, fetch GetItems with full flags (basic_info, release, platforms, assets, reviews, tag_count 10-20, extra_details) for that id only and store the ~3-10 KB result locally.
The capture path must never wait on the network: saving a backlog entry writes only the appid locally, and enrichment runs in the background.

Build image URLs only from API data: 'https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/' + asset_url_format.replace('${FILENAME}', file), with the host configurable (shared.fastly.steamstatic.com as alternative; avoid shared.cloudflare, which 301-redirects). Use library_capsule, then header, then a placeholder. Never guess library_600x900.jpg. Lazy-load covers and cache them forever, since URLs change when art changes.

Ship GetTagList (446 tags) and GetStoreCategories (72) as static per-language JSON and refresh weekly via version_hash. Hard-code a small genre-id table taken from appdetails samples, or show tags instead of genres.
Filter content descriptors 3 and 4 (adult-only, gratuitous sexual content) by default, with a user opt-in.
Do not use store /appreviews (retired 2026-10-22). Take the review summary from GetItems; use IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews only if review text is ever needed.
Use appdetails only on demand, for localized genre names or highlighted achievements, and parse dates from GetItems timestamps, never from appdetails' localized strings.

Architecture: because the APIs send no CORS headers, choose either Tauri (calls via tauri-plugin-http from Rust, scoped to api.steampowered.com, store.steampowered.com and *.steamstatic.com) or a PWA backed by a static snapshot on a CDN plus a small caching proxy for on-demand enrichment.
Throttle all Steam calls to at most 1 request per second with a single worker, exponential backoff and a global pause on 429, and keep a cached-only mode as fallback.

Raw probe outputs for reuse are in C:\Users\lucas\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-lucas-Documents-Programacion-GameAgenda\56497ade-bd80-409d-8199-9f2b9ba10c3e\scratchpad\research\R2\live (gi_all.json, gi250.json, pb800.bin, tags.json, cats.json, ad_bg3.json). The protobuf encoder and decoder are C:\Users\lucas\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-lucas-Documents-Programacion-GameAgenda\56497ade-bd80-409d-8199-9f2b9ba10c3e\scratchpad\scripts\pb.js and C:\Users\lucas\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-lucas-Documents-Programacion-GameAgenda\56497ade-bd80-409d-8199-9f2b9ba10c3e\scratchpad\scripts\pbdec.js.
risks: GetItems, appdetails, GetTagList and the CDN paths are undocumented for public use and can change without notice. Valve already removed ISteamApps/GetAppList and retired /appreviews on 2026-10-22.
Keyless per-IP rate limits are unknown. A central proxy or cron job puts every request on one IP, so a mass refresh could trigger 429s or temporary blocks.
Hashed asset paths change when developers update art. Covers cached with old URLs may eventually 404 or show outdated art (not verified), so a re-enrichment path is needed.
Requesting include_extra_details, full descriptions, trailers or screenshots in bulk inflates responses by 10-30x (up to ~30 KB per item) and could hit unknown response-size or time limits.
Review counts from GetItems cover Steam purchases only and were reported as 0 for a popular game at least once, so popularity ranking can be noisy.
About 4% of sampled items are adult-only (descriptors 3/4). Without default filtering they can surface in search results.
Removed apps (success 15) cannot be enriched at all. Their names and art must come from another source (R1 app list) or a placeholder.
Steam China (steam_realm 2, country CN) behavior was not tested and may differ.
Catalog size, and therefore snapshot size and call budget, depends on R1's real game count (150k here is an assumption).
open_questions: Is there a hard count cap on GetItems ids above 800 when using input_protobuf_encoded, and does adding format=json make it return JSON instead of binary protobuf?
What are the real keyless GetItems throttling thresholds (burst size, refill rate, block duration), and is a Retry-After header sent on 429?
Which coming_soon_display values do month, quarter and year release formats produce (date_month, date_quarter, date_year?), and what does steam_release_date contain for them?
Do old hashed asset URLs keep resolving after a developer replaces the art, and for how long?
What pixel dimensions do hashed '<sha1>/library_capsule.jpg' and library_capsule_2x actually have (presumably 600x900 and 1200x1800)?
Does IStoreQueryService/Query work without a key, and what are its page-size and paging limits for listing all coming-soon games?
Does GetItems ever hide region-locked items (unvailable_for_country_restriction) or adult-only items for some country_code values?
What exactly does 'assets' contain versus 'assets_without_overrides' (temporary event or sale art?), and which should a stable backlog cover use?
What do Valve's terms say about displaying Steam store art and data in a third-party app (outside this dimension)?

verdicts.evidence: GitHub API: SteamTracking commit 1978dcc003 was authored and committed 2025-11-13T22:05:17Z. It deletes both {name:GetAppList, version:1} and {version:2} from API/ISteamApps.json, and the current ISteamApps.json no longer lists GetAppList. The Steamworks isteamapps page has only the undated 'Deprecated - this API can no longer scale...' text. SteamAutoCracker #107 was opened 2025-11-16; the maintainer wrote on 2025-12-01 'It seems that Steam killed the endpoint'. The woctezuma README says 'As of November 25, 2025, this API is deprecated.' Live 2026-10-28: /ISteamApps/GetAppList/v1/ returned HTTP 404 'Method 'GetAppList' not found in interface 'ISteamApps''. Nuance: SteamTracking's dump also lists publisher-only methods, so it is Valve's full GetSupportedAPIList, not strictly the 'public' listing.

The Steamworks IStoreService page documents GET https://partner.steam-api.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/ with: key (required, 'Any web API key.'); if_modified_since; have_description_language ('Return only items that have a description in this language.'); include_games ('defaults to enabled'); include_dlc; include_software; include_videos ('videos and series'); include_hardware; last_appid; max_results ('Default 10k, max 50k.'). The page text on appid ordering, last_appid continuation, last_modified and price_change_number matches the claim word for word. SteamTracking API/IStoreService.json and xPaw api.json list the same 10 parameters. There are no include_demos, include_music or include_mods flags.

gofurry/steam-go storeservice v1.3.12 (published 2026-09-26) defines response.apps[] {appid, name, last_modified, price_change_number} plus have_more_results and last_appid. I downloaded jsnli data/games_appid.json (bot commit 6d30065, 2026-10-27T04:15:29Z): rows have exactly those 4 keys and appids are strictly ascending. Row 730 {Counter-Strike 2, 1793054556, 39840616} and row 5495700 {Too Many Chickens, 1793069391, 0} match the claim exactly.

The official parameter text says key = 'Any web API key.' jsnli calls https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?key=${STEAM_KEY}...&max_results=50000 and its bot commits daily (latest 2026-10-27T04:15:29Z; the dump's max last_modified is 04:14:24Z). SteamAutoCracker #117 (2026-03-17) has a user reporting that api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?key= 'still works'. The 2026-01-04 403 report in #107 used partner.steam-api.com. The Web API Overview says that host needs a publisher key: 'Requests made without a valid publisher key will return a 403', and such 403s 'will incur strict rate limits for the connecting IP'. So the open question in the claim is answered: the 403 came from using the wrong host.

verdicts.correction: These requirements hold: a domain name ('localhost' is acceptable per node-steamcommunity), accepting the ToU, a non-limited account (US$5 spent), and a Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator confirmation (error NoMobileDevice without one). Two parts need correcting. (1) 'One key per account' (2013 forum answer) is outdated: node-steamcommunity's createWebApiKey docs say registering again while a key exists creates a second key and 'both keys will continue working'. This is undocumented Valve behavior and may change. (2) The x-webapi-key request header is documented officially by Steamworks (Web API Overview > Authentication), not only by xPaw.
verdicts.evidence: steamcommunity.com/dev: you get a key from the /dev/apikey form and must accept the ToU. Several secondary sources confirm the limited-account rule (US$5, Web API blocked); the body of the Valve FAQ page did not render for me.

webui/common.proto (last commit 2026-10-22) has these StoreItem fields: success 3, visible 4, unvailable_for_country_restriction 5 (sic), name 6, store_url_path 7, type 10, is_free 13, is_early_access 14, content_descriptorids 20, release 31, is_coming_soon 34, best_purchase_option 40, unlisted 55. ValvePython EStoreAppType: Game 0, Demo 1, Mod 2, Movie 3, DLC 4, Guide 5, Software 6, Video 7, Series 8, Episode 9, Hardware 10, Music 11, Beta 12, Tool 13, Advertising 14, so the claim's subset is correct. Live: appid 1 returns success 15, visible false, name ''. 250 seven-digit ids per JSON call worked and 300 returned 400. Caveat: success 15 also covers region-locked items, which keep their name (see steamdata-X2).

Live GetItems ES: 50300, 1293830, 241560 and 271590 return success 1, visible true, the real name, unlisted true and no best_purchase_option. 19000 has best_purchase_option and no unlisted. appdetails?appids=50300 returns success:true with full data. The jsnli GetAppList dump lacks all four. Keyless Query (ES, sort 2, first 1,000 games, appids 10 to 71,250) also lacks 50300. mparmol README: removal requires invisibility in ES, US, JP and CN, and 'Querying only from Spain, 4 of 7 removal candidates turned out to be region blocks'.

Live with 'Origin: https://example.com': Query and GetItems (api.steampowered.com) and appdetails (store.steampowered.com) returned no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Nuance: the server-side conclusion holds for browser/PWA clients. A native client (Tauri/Rust) is not bound by CORS and could call the keyless endpoints, but must never carry a key.

I checked each input. 196,595 games / 50k per page = 4 GetAppList pages (the dump is 19.9 MB). Query returns 1000 per page, so 197 pages. Churn is 3,349 games/day (~140/hour). GetItems takes at least 250 ids per call, so 14-17 calls/day. The ToU cap is 100,000/day, so ~45 calls is ~0.045%. This is an estimate: the GetAppList calls cover games only (DLC etc. would need more), and keyless calls fall under undocumented per-IP limits, not the per-key cap.

Last common.proto commit: 2026-10-22T00:23:01Z. SteamTracking webui_enums: k_ESteamRealmGlobal = 1, k_ESteamRealmChina = 2. The Steamworks languages table has the API codes english, spanish, latam and schinese. Live keyless GET with input_json returned 200; ludarium PR #60 reports POST returns 405.

Adding country_code ES returned store_items. ES prices are formatted like '9,69€' (seen in Query best_purchase_option). ludarium PR #60 (opened 2026-09-17) reports the same empty 200. I did not re-test game_rating/PEGI.

For new games the hashed form dominates: among the 250 newest game appids (spanish context), library_capsule was '<sha1>/library_capsule.jpg' 243 times, '<sha1>/library_capsule_spanish.jpg' 6 and '<sha1>/library_capsule_latam.jpg' 1, with header present 250/250. Tauri v2 HTTP plugin docs: the Rust side is a reqwest re-export; the default permission allows no origins, so URLs must be allow-listed in capabilities (http:default allow/deny). The docs say nothing about CORS, so the Rust-side bypass remains an inference. Note: Steam's image CDN does send ACAO:* (see steamdata-X5).

Arkhemis PR #53 (2026-09-27) says it has been rate-limited per IP since 2026-09-24 (~270-request burst, ~0.96 req/s refill, ~4.5 min block, reproduced from VPS, VPN and residential IPs) and keeps using it behind a dedicated throttle. The rest holds: Valve publishes no number; azwrth13/QIT PR #19 (2026-09-29) only says 'keyless endpoints are throttled per IP'; the '1 request per 3 s' figure is not in that PR; free-steam-games-list PR #209 (2026-10-23) uses 50 games per request, ~2 minutes, daily.
verdicts.evidence: I fetched all three PRs. My own 20 spaced Steam requests today (GetItems, Query, appdetails, CDN) got no 429; the one 400 was the URL-length limit.

verdicts.correction: The catalog is ~196.6k games, not 150k: that is ~787 JSON GetItems calls at 250 ids or ~281 protobuf calls at 700 ids. Per-call size is also larger than estimated: the 250 newest appids with {include_assets, include_release} (best_purchase_option on by default) measured 421,704 B raw / 78,365 B gzip / 61,676 B brotli, about 2x the 210 KB / 37 KB figure, so plan for ~40-60 MB gzip. The keyless Query takes the same StoreBrowseItemDataRequest and returns up to 1000 store_items per call, so a bulk pass needs ~197 calls. The appdetails math (~62 h for 150k at 0.67 req/s) is correct.

The Web API Overview gives no numeric rate limits, only the partner-host 403 warning. The mparmol README says '~120 requests per ~5 min window, per IP' without naming the endpoint. SteamDB's Store Prices post (found via search; the site returns 403 to fetchers) carries a 2015 update capping appdetails at 200 requests per 5 minutes; I could not verify the month (July). SteamKit eresult.steamd: AccessDenied = 15, RateLimitExceeded = 84. Live: 200 responses carry X-eresult: 1. My 20 spaced Steam requests saw no 429.

verdicts.correction: TheGamer (2026-10-02, Sam Woods) attributes the 2025 total of 21,268 and its year-by-year table to SteamDB. The 2026 figure (20,220 through Oct 1) carries an asterisk as a partial year with no explicit source, and the 21,376 projection cites Games-Stats, not SteamDB. I did not check either number at SteamDB itself (403 to fetchers). tech-insider's 135,003 (2026-09-29) is unsourced. fredericksen (2024-07-08) reports 204,038 IDs on 2024-06-23 from an accumulated database, ~160 added and ~20 removed per day in June 2024.
verdicts.evidence: I fetched TheGamer, tech-insider and the fredericksen Substack. The SteamDB homepage and blog returned 403.

verdicts.correction: The API details are correct: steam-user 5.3.0 was published to npm 2025-12-04 and is the latest tag. getProductChanges and getProductInfo are 'Works when anonymous'. Going back more than 'around 5,000 changenumbers' returns only the current number; mparmol measured ~7,200 (~9.5 h). The EAppType and EAppReleaseState values are right (Unavailable 1, Prerelease 2, PreloadOnly 3, Released 4, Disabled 5). But 'exposes every app' is overstated: changes list every changed appid, while apps flagged needs_token/missingToken need an access token for most details, which an anonymous session may not get.

jsnli dump (196,595 games): 18 empty names. 866490 'TestApp', 639770 'UNTITLED' and 1025620 'Untitled' sit alongside 837470 'Untitled Goose Game' and 211970 'Test Drive: Ferrari Racing Legends'. 71 names contain the word 'demo' (case-insensitive word match), 4 contain 'soundtrack', 3 contain 'playtest'. 1640150 has last_modified 1710382377 (2024-03-14) and is text_tba live. Live: 866490 is success 1, type 0, with no assets and an empty release. appid 10 has [2,5]; HuniePop 339800 has [1,3,5,4] (order differs, same set). fredericksen (2024-08-06): id 5 = General Mature Content. The label for id 3 is still not confirmed from a primary source.

verdicts.correction: A 176-item sample overstates per-row cost and understates outliers. On the full GetAppList games dump (196,595 rows), [appid,name] measures 30.4 B raw / 13.4 B gzip / 9.7 B brotli per row: 5.98 MB / 2.64 MB / 1.91 MB in total. A 250-new-game sample of [appid,name,year,type] measured 35.9 B raw / 17.0 B gzip per row. Average name length is 17.6 B but the maximum is 542 B, not 51. Base totals on ~197k games, not 150k. The point that hashes compress badly stands.
verdicts.evidence: Measured locally with Node zlib (gzip level 9, brotli quality 11) on the downloaded jsnli dump and the live GetItems sample.

verdicts.correction: The cadence is a judgment call, but two inputs are wrong. (1) There are ~62.7k coming-soon games (62,686 live, 32% of games), not 10-20k. A daily refresh is ~251 GetItems JSON calls, or ~63 keyless Query calls using coming_soon_only + sort=2 at 1000 per page. (2) Treating 'success 15 twice' as removed misfires on region-locked SKUs, which return success 15 every time with unvailable_for_country_restriction=true and keep their appid and name. Only appid 0 with an empty name, or disappearance from GetAppList, signals removal. Also, Project Android was simply before its 01:00Z launch when sampled; that is not evidence of lag.
verdicts.evidence: Live Query count=0 with coming_soon_only. Live GetItems in ES/US on 21130, 24720, 19030, 11610, 19810 and 22490, and on 1 and 999999999.

verdicts.correction: The proto fields are right. But the annotation is not 'like GetItems': Query is 'bConstMethod=true, ePrivilege=1, eWebAPIKeyRequirement=1, rgBrowserAPISites=ArrayExpression', while GetItems lacks rgBrowserAPISites. What the claim calls untested is now verified live: keyless access returns HTTP 200; count is capped at 1000 (5000 requested gives 1000); sort=2 is strictly ascending by appid; released_only, coming_soon_only and type_filters work; any data_request returns full store_items with names. The rate limit is still unknown.
verdicts.evidence: Downloaded service_storequery.proto and service_storebrowse.proto and compared the RPC comments. Ran 9 keyless Query calls.

additional_findings.claim: Keyless IStoreQueryService/Query returns full StoreItem rows (localized name, type, content_descriptorids, categories, is_free, best_purchase_option) for 1000 games per call whenever any data_request is sent, so the whole game catalog with names can be built without a Steam Web API key in ~197 calls.
additional_findings.details: Live 2026-10-28 ~00:30Z, no key: input_json {query:{start:0,count:1000,sort:2,filters:{type_filters:{include_games:true}}},context:{language:'spanish',country_code:'ES'},data_request:{}} returned HTTP 200 with 1000 ids and 1000 store_items, every one named. 688,687 B raw, 63,251 B gzip (the server honors Accept-Encoding: gzip), 1.4 s. 196,615 ES games is ~197 pages, ~12-13 MB gzip. Without a data_request only ids come back (18 KB/page). The base catalog then needs no key (no $5 account, mobile authenticator or secret storage), but the method is undocumented (see X7).

additional_findings.claim: Query and GetItems filter by context.country_code: region-locked games drop out of Query, and GetItems returns them as success 15, visible false, unvailable_for_country_restriction true, with their appid and name kept; nonexistent ids return appid 0 and an empty name.
additional_findings.details: Live, country ES: the first sort=2 Query page (appids 10 to 71,250) lacked 16 of the 1,016 GetAppList games in that range, e.g. 11610 Dragon Nest, 19030 Rocket Knight, 21130 LEGO Harry Potter: Years 1-4, 22490 Fallout: New Vegas (regional SKU), 24720 SPORE Galactic Adventures. GetItems in ES on 5 of them, and in US on 22490, returned success 15 with unvailable_for_country_restriction true and the real name. Ids 1 and 999999999 returned appid 0 and name ''. Totals differ by country: 196,621 US vs 196,615 ES. Build the catalog from region-agnostic GetAppList or a union of countries, and never read success 15 alone as 'removed'.

additional_findings.claim: With language 'spanish', Query and GetItems return Spanish store names that differ from GetAppList's default names for ~0.5% of old games and ~4% of new ones, and GetAppList has no language parameter.
additional_findings.details: Live Query/GetItems (spanish) vs the 2026-10-27 GetAppList dump. 5 of the first 1,000 games differ, e.g. 24810 'Command & Conquer 3: La Ira de Kane' vs 'Command & Conquer™ 3: Kane’s Wrath', and 33610 'Broken Sword 3 - El Sueño del Dragón (2003)'. 11 of the 250 newest differ, e.g. 5421070 'Helado de Medianoche' vs 'Midnight Scoop', and 5422950 'Nada de holgazanes en mi orden' vs '宗门不养闲人'. The search index needs both the default and the localized name, plus normalized forms without ™, ® or punctuation, or searches in either language will miss games.

additional_findings.claim: The whole Steam game catalog as [appid, name] is 5.98 MB raw, 2.64 MB gzip and 1.91 MB brotli for 196,595 games, small enough to ship to the client for instant offline search.
additional_findings.details: Measured on jsnli/steamappidlist data/games_appid.json (GetAppList output, bot commit 2026-10-27T04:15Z, 19.9 MB as stored), as JSON [[appid,name],...]: 30.4 B raw / 13.4 B gzip-9 / 9.7 B brotli-11 per row. Average name 17.6 UTF-8 bytes, max 542 (truncate long names in the UI), 18 empty. Compressing the whole file beats per-row estimates from small samples (R2-23). Year, type and flag fields add a few bytes per row. Covers with 40-hex hashes are the costly part, so load them lazily or store the hashes as binary.

additional_findings.claim: Steam's image CDN (shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets) sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, unlike api.steampowered.com and store.steampowered.com/api, so a PWA can fetch and cache covers directly without a proxy.
additional_findings.details: Live HEAD on https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/730/162664aa5da85f418105350c5d67ca565f6c3713/header.jpg?t=1793054556 returned 200, 33,545 B, Last-Modified 2026-06-02, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The same day, GetItems, Query and appdetails responses had no ACAO. tags work either way. ACAO:* also allows readable fetch(), non-opaque Service Worker caching and canvas use, so no image proxy is needed. I checked only one host and one asset.

additional_findings.claim: Cover filenames depend on the request language and are hashed for new games: among the 250 newest game appids (language spanish), library_capsule was '<sha1>/library_capsule.jpg' 243 times, '<sha1>/library_capsule_spanish.jpg' 6 and '<sha1>/library_capsule_latam.jpg' 1.
additional_findings.details: Live GetItems (ES, spanish, include_assets) on the 250 newest game appids from 5,420,790 (248 coming soon): header and library_capsule were present for all 250, all under a 40-hex folder. So the snapshot should store the cover path per UI language, or always request one fixed language. Expect hashed paths for every new game, and never guess hash-less URLs: 5338720 library_600x900.jpg returned 404.

additional_findings.claim: The keyless store services sit outside Valve's documented Web API: SteamTracking's GetSupportedAPIList dump has no IStoreQueryService or IStoreBrowseService, xPaw tags Query and GetItems 'undocumented' with key marked required, and steamcommunity.com/dev says 'All use of the Steam Web API requires the use of an API Key'.
additional_findings.details: Checked 2026-10-28: SteamTracking API/IStoreQueryService.json and API/IStoreBrowseService.json return 404, while API/IStoreService.json lists GetAppList with the documented params. xPaw api.json gives both methods _type 'undocumented' and lists key as required. Valve already removed ISteamApps/GetAppList in Nov 2025 with no dated notice. Plan: treat keyless Query/GetItems as best-effort, keep a keyed IStoreService/GetAppList path as fallback, and always serve the app from its own cached snapshot.
