researches.label: Steam account, auth, legal
researches.summary: Steam should be an optional, import-only layer over a local-first to-play list. IDENTITY: Steam offers third parties only OpenID 2.0 (no OIDC; OAuth Client IDs only for Valve-chosen Cloud/Workshop partners). OpenID needs no secret; verify server-side via check_authentication POST to a hardcoded steamcommunity.com URL (CVE-2026-82183, Sept 2026, shows the cost of skipping it). Leanest hardened Node lib: steam-signin 1.0.5 (no key, returns only SteamID). Tauri: system browser + loopback (tauri-plugin-oauth) or hosted HTTPS return_to bouncing to a deep link; custom-scheme return_to untested after login. Public data needs no login: a pasted /profiles/<id> or /id/<vanity>/?xml=1 (keyless, live) suffices; OpenID matters only when a server stores data per Steam user. DATA: GetOwnedGames (key) -> 'comprado' + playtime, only if 'Game details' privacy is Public (else HTTP 200 {"response":{}}); family_shared is not 'comprado'. Wishlist is keyless (GetWishlist; GetWishlistSortedFiltered also fills Spanish store data per page) -> 'quiero jugar' suggestions. Achievements: keyless GetUserAchievements + GetGameAchievements give per-set completion -> 'platinado' at ~1 call/game; no batch endpoint works with a plain key. Achievement Sets beta (Oct 2026) redefines 100% (archived excluded, DLC sets separate, completed stays completed). ARCHITECTURE: api.steampowered.com sends no CORS headers and keys cannot ship in clients -> a small backend/proxy is mandatory for a PWA and for keyed calls from Tauri. 100k calls/day/key; IP-level 429s reported; scans must be user-triggered, incremental (rtime_last_played), cached (schema_hash). LEGAL: API ToU (2010): confidential key, privacy policy, disclose stored Steam Data + storage countries, retrieve only as the user requests, personal use, no nofollow, no implied endorsement, revocable, silent on commercial use. Use Valve's sign-in buttons + trademark notice. No user session tokens, no PICS. Images: CDN allows hotlinking (ACAO *); hotlink rather than re-host, disclose IP sharing. GDPR: SteamID + play data are personal data; basis Art. 6(1)(b); minimise; export/delete; RoPA; Spanish consent age 14 (bill to 16 pending); auth cookies exempt, analytics need consent, same for localStorage. Live-test raw outputs: C:\Users\lucas\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-lucas-Documents-Programacion-GameAgenda\56497ade-bd80-409d-8199-9f2b9ba10c3e\scratchpad\research\r3

findings.claim: Steam offers third-party sites/apps only OpenID 2.0 sign-in (OP endpoint https://steamcommunity.com/openid/login); there is no OpenID Connect, and Steam OAuth Client IDs are issued by Valve only to partners that need cross-platform Cloud sync or Workshop.
findings.details: Partner doc: 'Steam is an OpenID Provider, as described in the OpenID 2.0 specification'; claimed ID http(s)://steamcommunity.com/openid/id/<steamid64>. Live XRDS (GET https://steamcommunity.com/openid with Accept: application/xrds+xml, 2026-10-28): Type http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0/server, URI https://steamcommunity.com/openid/login. OAuth doc (undated): Client ID must come from Valve; 'if you are not planning on supporting cross-platform Cloud sync or Workshop support, we will not provide you with a Client ID'; scopes read_cloud/write_cloud per AppId; token_type=steam. OpenID yields identity only (SteamID64): no scopes, no access to private data. Auth.js lists no Steam provider.

findings.claim: The login redirect sends openid.ns=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0, openid.mode=checkid_setup, openid.claimed_id and openid.identity = http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0/identifier_select, openid.realm and openid.return_to; verification is a server-side POST of the returned fields with openid.mode=check_authentication to https://steamcommunity.com/openid/login, which replies in key-value text with is_valid:true or is_valid:false.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: POST with a forged openid.sig -> HTTP 200 text/plain 'ns:http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0\nis_valid:false'. Pass back openid.assoc_handle, openid.signed, openid.sig plus every field named in openid.signed (Steam typically signs signed,op_endpoint,claimed_id,identity,return_to,response_nonce,assoc_handle; not observed with a real login here). Pre-login, Steam 302-redirects to /openid/loginform/?goto=... (200 'Sign In'). Claimed ID is documented as http:// (partner doc) and https:// (steamcommunity.com/dev): accept both. Login itself needs no client secret or API key.

findings.claim: Relying parties that skip check_authentication or trust the asserted op_endpoint are fully bypassable; a safe verifier POSTs to a hardcoded steamcommunity.com URL, requires claimed_id, return_to and response_nonce inside openid.signed, matches return_to to its own URL, regex-checks claimed_id and accepts each assertion only once.
findings.details: CVE-2026-82183 (published Sept 2026, CVSS 8.1): WordPress 'OAuth Single Sign On' plugin <7.0.1 trusted Steam callback params without check_authentication -> attacker logs in as any non-admin user. GHSA-hhw9-35p2-q2c5 (2021-01-29, Critical): socialiteproviders/steam <1.1 accepted assertions from an attacker's own OpenID server. OpenID 2.0 s11.1: return_to scheme/authority/path MUST match; s11.4.2.1: OP 'MUST NOT issue more than one verification response for each authentication response' (anti-replay). OpenID 2.0 has no 'state': put a random value in return_to's query (it is signed) bound to a short-lived cookie to stop login-CSRF (inference). SteamID is public, never a secret.

findings.claim: steam-signin 1.0.5 (DoctorMcKay, published 2025-02-12, sole dependency steamid ^2.0.0) is the leanest hardened option and needs no API key; passport-steam's last release is 1.0.18 (2023-06-18); node-steam-openid 2.0.0 (2024-11-23) requires an API key and fetches the full profile; Auth.js and Better Auth ship no official Steam provider.
findings.details: npm registry checked 2026-10-28. steam-signin source: hardcoded POST to steamcommunity.com/openid/login, rejects unless claimed_id/return_to/response_nonce are signed, checks return_to realm, regex ^https?://steamcommunity.com/openid/id/(\d+)/?$, returns a SteamID object, no key. node-steam-openid: constructor throws without apiKey; always calls GetPlayerSummaries (incl. realname) + GetProfileItemsEquipped; deps axios, openid ^2.0.6. openid (node-openid) 2.0.18 published 2026-09-08. next-auth-steam 0.4.0 (2024-12-09, NextAuth v4-style API). Better Auth: only a demo repo with a custom plugin. passport-steam: 15 open issues, 8 open PRs.

findings.topic: Login from a Tauri desktop app or a PWA
findings.claim: Because OpenID 2.0 needs no client secret, a Tauri app can sign in through the system browser with a loopback callback (tauri-plugin-oauth v2) or with an HTTPS return_to on a server that then bounces to a deep link (tauri-plugin-deep-link v2); a PWA uses the normal web redirect with server-side verification.
findings.details: Live pre-login test 2026-10-28: Steam accepted realm http://127.0.0.1:53682 and gameagenda://auth alike (302 -> loginform, 200 'Sign In'); whether the positive assertion is delivered to a custom scheme after login is UNTESTED. OpenID s9.2: return_to scheme and port must equal the realm's. Tauri deep-link docs (updated 2026-06-15): Windows registers schemes at install, register_all() for dev, URLs arrive as CLI args anyone can forge -> validate; pair with single-instance plugin. If a backend trusts the identity, the backend must run check_authentication (forward the full query; Steam verifies each assertion once). passport-steam's example realm http://localhost:3000 shows localhost works.

findings.topic: Browser access and API key confidentiality
findings.claim: api.steampowered.com returns no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and Web API keys must stay server-side, so a PWA cannot call the Steam Web API directly from the browser; any Steam integration needs a backend or serverless proxy (Tauri can call keyless endpoints from Rust).
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: GET IWishlistService/GetWishlistItemCount with 'Origin: https://gameagenda.example' -> 200 with only Content-Type, Expires and 'Cache-Control: max-age=0, no-cache, no-store' (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin) -> a browser fetch from another origin is blocked by CORS. Steamworks: keys 'must be stored securely, and must not be distributed with a game client'; send over HTTPS; key may go in the 'x-webapi-key' header. ToU: keep the key confidential, share with no third party. Because Steam responds no-store, the proxy must add its own cache. By contrast, CDN images return ACAO * (R3-21).

findings.claim: IPlayerService/GetOwnedGames/v1 requires a key (live: HTTP 401 without one) and takes steamid, include_appinfo, include_played_free_games, appids_filter, include_free_sub, skip_unvetted_apps (default true), language, include_extended_appinfo, include_family_licenses and include_all_free_games.
findings.details: Response: game_count + games[]: appid, name, playtime_forever, playtime_2weeks, playtime_windows/mac/linux/deck_forever, playtime_disconnected, rtime_last_played (Unix), img_icon_url (hash), has_community_visible_stats, capsule_filename, sort_as, has_workshop/market/dlc/leaderboards, content_descriptorids, family_shared. include_extended_appinfo needs include_appinfo; include_family_licenses adds family-shared games flagged family_shared (not 'comprado'); include_all_free_games only if playtime is visible; free games excluded by default. Playtime in minutes (tracked since ~2009, community). Profile-limited games reportedly need skip_unvetted_apps=false.

findings.claim: Owned games, playtime, wishlist and achievements are returned only when the user's Steam 'Game details' privacy lets the caller see them (in practice Public for a server-held key); otherwise calls return HTTP 200 with an empty {"response":{}}, so importing 'comprado' requires the user to set Game details to Public.
findings.details: Partner doc: GetOwnedGames 'Returns a list of games owned by the player if their owned games/game details are visible to you.' Valve's April 2018 privacy update: 'Game details' covers owned + wishlisted games, achievements and playtime; libraries hidden by default; total playtime can be hidden separately. Community (Sept 2026): key-based endpoints 'see the profile the way a stranger does'. Empty bodies are ambiguous (protobuf JSON omits empty fields; intermittent empties on public profiles also reported) -> check communityvisibilitystate (1 = not visible, 3 = public) or XML privacyState and show a 'set Game details to Public' guide.

findings.claim: ISteamUser/GetPlayerSummaries v2 (key; up to 100 comma-separated steamids), IPlayerService/GetRecentlyPlayedGames v1 (key, steamid, count where 0 = all) and ISteamUser/ResolveVanityURL v1 (key, vanityurl, url_type 1 = profile, 2 = group, 3 = official game group) all require a Web API key.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: ResolveVanityURL without key -> HTTP 400 'Required parameter 'key' is missing'. GetPlayerSummaries public fields: steamid, personaname, profileurl, avatar/avatarmedium/avatarfull, personastate, communityvisibilitystate, profilestate, lastlogoff, commentpermission; visible-only fields: realname, primaryclanid, timecreated, gameid, gameextrainfo, loccountrycode, locstatecode, loccityid. For data minimisation request it only if the UI shows persona name/avatar, and do not persist location/realname.

findings.claim: A pasted vanity profile URL can be resolved without key or login via https://steamcommunity.com/id/<vanity>/?xml=1, which returned steamID64, privacyState and visibilityState; the legacy /games?tab=all&xml=1 library export now redirects to the login page.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: /id/xpaw/?xml=1 -> 200 text/xml with <steamID64>76561197972494985</steamID64>, <privacyState>public</privacyState>, <visibilityState>3</visibilityState> and avatar URLs. /profiles/76561197972494985/games?tab=all&xml=1 -> 302 to /login/. URLs of the form /profiles/<17-digit id> need no resolution at all. Caveat: undocumented legacy community endpoint with no SLA; call only on explicit user action and fall back to ResolveVanityURL through the backend key. Without login anyone can paste someone else's public profile; the ToU says to retrieve a user's data only 'as requested by the end user' (interpretation needed).

findings.claim: IWishlistService/GetWishlist/v1/?steamid=<id> works without a key and returns items[{appid, priority, date_added}] for public profiles, GetWishlistItemCount returns {count}, and the legacy store.steampowered.com/wishlist/profiles/<id>/wishlistdata/ endpoint is gone.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: public profile 76561197972494985 -> 200, 47 items, priority 0-54 (9 items at 0; semantics undocumented, likely user ranking with 0 = unranked), date_added Unix (2020-11-03 to 2026-08-25). 76561197960287930 -> 200 {"response":{}} (private vs empty indistinguishable). Legacy wishlistdata URL -> 302 to https://store.steampowered.com/. Protobuf annotation eWebAPIKeyRequirement=1 matches the keyless IStoreBrowseService/GetItems, while key-only GetOwnedGames has =2 (useful heuristic). No Steamworks doc -> may change without notice. Visibility follows 'Game details' privacy.

findings.topic: Wishlist with localized store data in one call
findings.claim: IWishlistService/GetWishlistSortedFiltered (keyless) returns the whole wishlist sorted but fills store_item (localized name, description, assets, best_purchase_option with final_price_in_cents) only for items within [start_index, start_index+page_size), page_size defaulting to 100.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: input_json {"steamid":"76561197972494985","context":{"language":"spanish","country_code":"ES"},"data_request":{"include_basic_info":true,"include_assets":true},"page_size":2} -> 200, 47 items, 2 with store_item (e.g. 'DOOM: The Dark Ages' with Spanish short_description, publishers, assets.asset_url_format, best_purchase_option). Proto also offers filters (only_games, exclude_early_access, max_price_in_cents...), category_ids (wishlist categories) and share_token. Lets an import show Spanish names and covers without extra GetItems calls.

findings.claim: IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements (steamid, appid) and IPlayerService/GetGameAchievements (appid, language) currently work without a key and return per-achievement unlock state plus per-set completion (groups[].is_completed, time_completed), enough to detect 100% with about one call per game.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28, Portal 2 (620), public profile: 51 achievements, all unlocked:true with unlock_time; groups 1 'Cooperativo' 22/22 and 2 'Un jugador' 29/29 is_completed:true; group 0 holds 0 achievements and reports is_completed:false (ignore empty groups). GetGameAchievements (language=spanish): localized_name/desc, icon, hidden, player_percent_unlocked ('74.0'), groupid, archived; groups[].dlcappid/total_achievements; schema_version/schema_hash for caching. xPaw marks both 'undocumented'. Documented fallback with key: ISteamUserStats/GetPlayerAchievements v1 (key, steamid, appid, l) + GetSchemaForGame v2 (key, appid, l).

findings.topic: No library-wide batch endpoint usable with a plain key
findings.claim: No key-only batch endpoint yields library-wide completion: GetTopAchievementsForGames (key; steamid, language, max_achievements up to 8, appids[]) returns total_achievements plus at most 8 top unlocked achievements but no unlocked count, GetAchievementsProgress (unlocked/total/all_unlocked per app) rejects plain keys, and GetGamesWithAchievementProgress returns 404 on the public Web API.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: GetTopAchievementsForGames without key -> 401 'verify your key= parameter'; keyless GET GetGamesWithAchievementProgress -> 404. Proto GetAchievementsProgress response: appid, unlocked, total, percentage, all_unlocked, cache_time, vetted, groups_completed_base/dlc, base_game_total. Community (achievement-battle README; barryjj PR merged 2026-09-23): a plain key gets unauthorized; it works only with the account's own access token, 'one POST per 100 apps'. Conclusion: 100% detection costs ~1 call per achievement-enabled game.

findings.claim: Obtaining other users' Steam access/refresh tokens (e.g. via steam-session credential or QR login) to read private data or batched achievement progress is outside sanctioned use: the library's author forbids it, the API ToU forbids intercepting or storing Steam passwords, and the SSA forbids letting others use your account.
findings.details: steam-session README (DoctorMcKay): 'This is for use with your own accounts.' and it 'is not to be used to authenticate other Steam users or to gain access to their accounts', pointing to Steam OpenID instead. Web API ToU: you must not intercept or store users' Steam passwords. SSA (last updated 2026-09-10) s1.C: 'You may not reveal, share or otherwise allow others to use your password or Account.' Refresh tokens carry web-session power over the account, a major breach liability. Only OpenID + public data is a clean path.

findings.claim: With the ToU cap of 100,000 Web API calls/day per key and about one call per achievement-enabled game for 100% detection, a full scan of a 500-game library costs roughly 300 calls, so scans must be user-triggered, incremental and cached, and the backend must cope with HTTP 429 throttling.
findings.details: Example (inference): a 500-game library with ~300 has_community_visible_stats apps costs ~1 GetOwnedGames + ~300 achievement calls, i.e. ~330 full scans/day per key. Incremental syncs only need apps whose rtime_last_played/playtime_2weeks changed (a completed set 'stays completed' even if achievements are added). Cache schemas by schema_hash. Keyless endpoints spend no key quota but appear IP-throttled: community reports (Apr-Jun 2025) of 429 every 10-20 min at 1 req/120 s, attributed to per-IP/shadow limits; shared serverless IPs make it worse. Use a queue + exponential backoff; never retry 401.

findings.claim: Under Steam's Achievement Sets beta (press 2026-10-16), completing a set means unlocking every still-available achievement in it: archived achievements are not required, DLC sets count only for DLC owners, and a completed set stays completed if achievements are added later.
findings.details: Steamworks ach_guide: every game has an undeletable 'Base game achievements' set; sets are open to all players or tied to one DLC; limits 40 sets/app and 5,000 achievements/app (100 if unvetted). Press (Engadget, VGC, 2026-10-16): beta, 17 games incl. Portal 2, L4D2, TF2, Forza Horizon 5; 'set complete' trophy. API mapping (live): GetGameAchievements groups[].dlcappid/archived and GetUserAchievements groups[].is_completed/time_completed. Suggest 'platinado' = base set (dlcappid 0) completed, optional '100% con DLC'. A naive unlocked == total check can disagree with Steam's UI.

findings.topic: Steam Web API Terms of Use
findings.claim: The Steam Web API Terms of Use (last updated July 2010) cap usage at 100,000 calls/day and require a confidential key, a privacy policy for nonpublic end-user data, telling users which Steam Data is stored and in which countries, and retrieving a user's data only as that user requests.
findings.details: Quotes: 'You are limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day.'; 'You will post a privacy policy regarding the use of nonpublic end user data (including such Steam Data)'; 'You will inform the end user about any Steam Data you will store'; 'you will store the Steam Data in a country (or countries) identified in your privacy policy'; 'You will only retrieve Steam Data about a Steam end user as requested by the end user'. License: distribute Steam Data 'to end users for their personal use via your Application'. Also: no 'nofollow' on Valve links, no implied endorsement, revocable anytime, delete Steam Data on exit, Washington law, silent on commercial use.

findings.topic: Obtaining a Steam Web API key
findings.claim: Officially a user Web API key needs only a Steam account and a domain name (steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey), but Steam reportedly refuses keys to accounts without Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator or without games (community reports 2024-2025).
findings.details: Steamworks: 'The standard user keys are available to everyone' and need only 'a Steam account and the domain name that will be associated with this key'. Error texts reported 2024-11-11: 'Your account does not meet the requirements for a developer API key. Your account requires Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator.' and 'You will be granted access to Steam Web API keys when you have games in your Steam account.' A June 2025 thread repeats that new keys require Steam Guard. Implication: bring-your-own-key (each user creates a key) adds heavy friction, contrary to 'rapida y agil'; prefer one server-held key.

findings.topic: Branding, sign-in buttons and app naming
findings.claim: Valve asks OpenID sites to use its 'Sign in through Steam' button images, forbids implying endorsement or making Steam marks primary or prominent, and allows only stating that you implemented the API, so a neutral name such as 'GameAgenda' with an attribution notice is the safe pattern.
findings.details: Buttons (steamcommunity.com/dev): https://community.akamai.steamstatic.com/public/images/signinthroughsteam/sits_01.png and sits_02.png; partner doc also lists sits_large_border.png, sits_large_noborder.png, sits_small.png. Branding page: marks 'may not be displayed as primary or prominent features on any non-Valve materials'; logo only from approved artwork, stand-alone; Valve may ask to modify or remove uses. Attribution: 'Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Valve Corporation...'. ToU: claiming any relationship beyond having implemented the API needs Valve's prior written approval. Keep 'Steam' out of the app name and icon.

findings.claim: Steam's CDN serves store images to third-party referers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and ~10-year public caching, so hotlinking and client-side caching work technically; legally, hotlinking freely available images is lower-risk in the EU than re-hosting copies, but it discloses users' IP addresses to Valve's CDN.
findings.details: Live HEAD shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/730/<hash>/header.jpg?t=1793054556 with Referer gameagenda.example -> 200 image/jpeg 33,545 B, Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, Cache-Control public, max-age=315269018. Images are publishers' copyrighted assets; no Valve doc licenses them to third parties beyond the ToU's 'Steam Data... personal use' (inference). CJEU Svensson/BestWater: linking/embedding freely accessible works is no new public; Renckhoff C-161/17 (2018): re-posting a copy is a new communication. LG Munchen I 3 O 17493/20 (2022): EUR 100 for sending visitor IPs to Google Fonts without legal basis -> name the CDN in the privacy policy.

findings.topic: Steam client protocol (PICS) and the Subscriber Agreement
findings.claim: No Valve document authorizes third-party services to use the Steam client protocol (PICS via SteamKit2/node-steam-user, including anonymous logins); the SSA (last updated 2026-09-10) bars emulating Valve's network protocols, reverse engineering and bots, so PICS is a tolerated gray zone rather than a sanctioned API.
findings.details: SSA s2.G: no reverse engineering, and no emulating or redirecting 'the communication protocols used by Valve in any network feature'; s4.C: no 'scripts, bots, macros, or other non-human-controlled systems'; s2.A licence is for 'personal, non-commercial use'. Anonymous logins involve no subscriber account, so applicability is debatable (inference), but Valve can block IPs at will. EU/UK subscribers: law of habitual residence applies. For R3: never log users in over the CM protocol; stick to the Web API + OpenID.

findings.topic: GDPR status of SteamID and play data; lawful basis; minimisation
findings.claim: A SteamID64 and the library, playtime, wishlist and achievements linked to it are personal data (GDPR Art. 4(1) 'online identifier'; it resolves to a public profile), and the user-requested import can rest on Art. 6(1)(b) (contract) rather than consent, subject to strict data minimisation.
findings.details: EDPB Guidelines 2/2019: Art. 6(1)(b) covers only processing objectively necessary for the service the user requested. Minimise: store steamid64 + per-app status/playtime/timestamps; skip realname, location fields and raw API payloads (node-steam-openid pulls realname by default; steam-signin returns only the ID). Not special-category data. Storage limitation: delete imported Steam Data when the user disconnects Steam (also ToU termination clause). Local-first (data only on device, no developer server) shrinks controller duties, but GDPR Recital 18 still covers providers of the means, so keep a privacy notice (inference).

findings.topic: Spain/EU obligations: notice, rights, RoPA, minors, transfers
findings.claim: A Spain-based operator must give Art. 13 GDPR information (layered per LOPDGDD Art. 11: identity, purpose and rights 15-22 in the first layer), answer access/erasure/portability requests within one month (Art. 12(3)), keep a record of processing (the Art. 30(5) SME exemption does not cover non-occasional processing) and treat 14 as the current age of digital consent (LOPDGDD Art. 7).
findings.details: BOE consolidated LOPDGDD (updated 27/12/2025) still says 14; bill 121/000052 (BOCG Apr 2025) would raise it to 16, final approval not confirmed. AEPD tools: Facilita RGPD (low-risk processing; generates information clauses, processor clauses, RoPA and a security annex) and Facilita Emprende (2020; startups incl. 'desarrollo de juegos o aplicaciones web'). Portability: export JSON/CSV. Transfers: EU-US DPF still in force (General Court T-553/23 dismissed 2025-09-03; appeal C-703/25 P pending); EU hosting avoids that risk and simplifies the ToU 'countries' clause.

findings.claim: Under LSSI-CE art. 22.2 as read by the AEPD cookie guide (updated May 2024), session/authentication, user-input and UI-preference (e.g. language) cookies need no consent while analytics cookies do, 'Reject' must be as prominent as 'Accept' (mandatory since 11 Jan 2024), and the same rules apply to localStorage/IndexedDB.
findings.details: AEPD guide: analytics 'no estan exentas del deber de obtener un consentimiento' but are low-risk if first-party, aggregated, statistical, disclosed, with opt-out. Exempt list (GT29 WP194): user-input, session-only authentication, user-security, media-player session, load-balancing and UI-customisation cookies. WP194: 'Persistent login cookies which store an authentication token across browser sessions are not exempted'; a 'remember me' checkbox counts as consent. EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 v2 (adopted 2024-10-07): Art. 5(3) ePrivacy covers any storage/access on the terminal. An app using only exempt storage needs no consent banner.

recommendations: Keep Steam optional and import-only: capturing a game to the to-play list (search + one tap 'Quiero jugar') must work offline/local with no login. Run the Steam import as a background job that pre-fills statuses.

Offer two entry points. For a local-first MVP: 'Pegar perfil de Steam' (SteamID64 or vanity, no login; use /profiles/<id> directly, resolve vanity through backend ResolveVanityURL with ?xml=1 as fallback). Add 'Iniciar sesion con Steam' (OpenID via steam-signin) only once server-side sync or accounts exist.

Run a thin backend or serverless proxy that holds the single Web API key (x-webapi-key header, secret store). It should add caching (Steam responds no-store), per-user quotas, a request queue with exponential backoff on 429, and health checks plus feature flags for undocumented endpoints. Never ship the key in the Tauri binary or the PWA bundle.

OpenID checklist: hardcoded check_authentication POST to https://steamcommunity.com/openid/login; require claimed_id, return_to and response_nonce in openid.signed; exact return_to match; claimed_id regex ^https?://steamcommunity\.com/openid/id/(\d{17})/?$; a random state in return_to bound to an httpOnly cookie; reject reused nonces; then issue the app's own session.

Tauri: always use the system browser, never an embedded webview login. Prefer a hosted HTTPS return_to plus a one-time code delivered by deep link (tauri-plugin-deep-link + single-instance), or a loopback callback via tauri-plugin-oauth. Test a custom-scheme return_to manually before relying on it.

Status mapping: call GetOwnedGames (include_appinfo, include_played_free_games, skip_unvetted_apps=false, include_extended_appinfo). Mark 'comprado' only for owned apps that are not family_shared; played F2P games go to 'en biblioteca'. Turn the wishlist into suggested 'quiero jugar' items the user confirms. Use playtime_forever and rtime_last_played as 'jugando'/'jugado' hints.

Platinado: make the scan user-triggered and limit it to has_community_visible_stats apps. Use keyless GetUserAchievements groups (base set dlcappid=0 is_completed), falling back to GetPlayerAchievements + GetSchemaForGame with the key. Re-check only apps whose rtime_last_played changed, cache schemas by schema_hash, and keep a manual override because Achievement Sets semantics may change.
Detect private profiles up front (communityvisibilitystate or XML privacyState). Show a short Spanish guide to set 'Detalles de juegos: Publico' instead of silently importing an empty library.

Compliance pack before launch: a Spanish, layered privacy policy listing the Steam Data stored, purposes, storage countries (prefer EU hosting) and processors (hosting, Steam CDN for images). Add in-app JSON/CSV export and 'Desconectar Steam y borrar datos', a RoPA via AEPD Facilita RGPD/Emprende, a minimum age of 14 (or 16 to be safe), the trademark notice and the Valve sign-in button, and no rel=nofollow on Steam links.

Data minimisation: persist only steamid64 plus appid-level status, playtime and timestamps. Do not persist realname, location or raw API payloads, and prefer steam-signin over node-steam-openid (which fetches realname).

Cookies: use only an httpOnly session cookie (exempt) plus an optional 'Mantener sesion iniciada' checkbox. Avoid third-party analytics, or gate them behind a banner with equally prominent Accept and Reject. Treat localStorage and IndexedDB the same way.
Do not use PICS/SteamKit, Steam user access or refresh tokens, or scraping of community pages beyond the explicit ?xml=1 vanity lookup.
risks: The keyless endpoints relied on (IWishlistService/GetWishlist, IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements and GetGameAchievements, steamcommunity ?xml=1) are undocumented. They can change or start requiring a key without notice, and under the ToU Valve can revoke API access at any time.
Per-IP throttling (HTTP 429, with reported multi-hour shadow limits) on shared serverless egress IPs could stall imports for all users at once.
Since 2018 Steam hides game details by default, so many imports will come back empty and frustrate users unless the UX explains the setting.
Achievement Sets have been in beta since Oct 2026. Completion semantics and the API group fields may change, so 'platinado' could stop matching Steam's own UI.
OpenID 2.0 is legacy and its libraries are thinly maintained (passport-steam's last release was 2023). Misconfigured verifiers are a recurring CVE pattern (CVE-2026-82183).
How Steam handles a custom-scheme return_to after login is unverified, so a Tauri flow built on it could break.
The ToU date from 2010 and say nothing about commercial use; monetisation (ads or subscriptions) could conflict with the 'personal use' licence.
Hotlinking Steam CDN images sends user IPs to Valve's CDN, a GDPR exposure (cf. the Munich Google Fonts ruling). Re-hosting copies instead raises copyright exposure (Renckhoff).
Spain's minors bill may raise the digital-consent age from 14 to 16. The EU-US DPF faces a pending CJEU appeal (C-703/25 P) and a threatened noyb challenge, which affects US hosting.
The developer reportedly needs a Steam account with games and Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator to obtain the server key.
If users can paste any profile without logging in, the app may fetch data about third parties that was not 'requested by the end user', a gray area under both the ToU and GDPR.
open_questions: Will GameAgenda have server-side accounts and sync (which needs OpenID, a backend and fuller GDPR duties), or start local-first with an optional profile paste?
Is the MVP desktop (Tauri), PWA or both? This decides loopback/deep link versus a plain web redirect, and whether keyless calls can skip the proxy.
Does Steam deliver positive assertions to a custom-scheme or 127.0.0.1 return_to after a real login? This needs a manual test with a real account.
Do keyless IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements calls share the per-IP limits of keyed calls, and what sustained rate is safe? This needs a controlled test.
Should 'platinado' mean the base set only, or 100% including DLC sets? This is a product decision now that Achievement Sets exist.
Is monetisation planned? The 2010 ToU say nothing about commercial use, so consider asking Valve before charging.
PlayStation trophies ('platinado' implies PSN): there is no public PSN API for third parties, so this needs separate research (unofficial NPSSO-token libraries carry ToS risk).
Wishlist 'priority' semantics (does 0 mean unranked?) are undocumented. Confirm before mapping them to an in-app order.
What is the status of the Spanish minors bill (121/000052) in late 2026? Has the age-of-consent change to 16 been enacted?

researches.label: third-party & multi-platform sources
researches.summary: For the later multi-platform phase, IGDB is the only source that combines all-platform coverage (PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, retro), a free licence for non-commercial AND commercial use (commercial = free partnership + visible attribution), explicit permission to cache/mirror ('we prefer if you store and serve the data'), webhooks for incremental sync, and a documented Steam crosswalk (external_games: external_game_source=1, uid=appid; also GOG 5, Microsoft 11, Xbox 31, Epic 26, PS Store US 36). Constraints: Twitch client-credentials, 4 req/s, 8 open requests, 500 items/request, no CORS, so it must sit behind a backend; CSV dumps only for partners. IGDB also has time-to-beat (hastily/normally/completely, seconds) that replaces HowLongToBeat, and game_type/version_parent/game_status (rumored, cancelled, early access) to collapse editions and list upcoming games. Wikidata (CC0) is a free offline crosswalk: live counts today show ~129k items with a Steam appid (91% also carry an IGDB ID), ~129k ITAD, ~126k SteamGridDB, 77k MobyGames, 61k RAWG, 49k HLTB, but only ~6k each for PS Store, Nintendo eShop and Microsoft Store and ~2.5k Epic; IDs are often slugs and multi-valued (Hades: IGDB 'hades--1', 3 MobyGames ids), so identity must be many-to-many. Prices/deals: ITAD API needs an app key (no fees listed), allows commercial use if the app is public, 1000 req/5 min, Steam appid lookup (keyless /lookup/id/shop/61/v1 worked live), but its terms forbid apps that 'compete' with ITAD projects (it has Waitlist/Collection) and any data alteration. Avoid or deprioritise: Giant Bomb (API offline after leaving Fandom, live check), HowLongToBeat (no API; unofficial endpoints moved repeatedly and 429s since Sept 2026), MobyGames (paid: ~$9.99/mo hobby, $99.99+/mo commercial), RAWG (key, 20k req/month free with a backlink on every page, redistribution banned, ~$149/mo business), SteamGridDB (no PS/Xbox, terms bar automated use), SteamSpy (stale: still names 730 'Counter-Strike: Global Offensive', playtime 0), PCGamingWiki (CC BY-NC-SA). User progress: PSN trophies only via reverse-engineered NPSSO APIs that conflict with PSN ToS 10.7/5.1 (ban risk), so 'platinado' must be a manual flag (optional local-only import at most); Xbox via OpenXBL (unofficial, free 150 req/h, $5-35/mo); RetroAchievements free key. GOG/Epic have no official catalog APIs (their JSON feeds answer keyless but are undocumented). Manual/custom games are required for speed and coverage gaps.

findings.claim: IGDB API v4 needs Twitch app credentials (OAuth2 client_credentials), allows 4 requests/second and at most 8 open requests (429 when exceeded), and rejects browser calls (no CORS), so it must be called from a backend.
findings.details: [doc] Token: POST https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token?client_id=..&client_secret=..&grant_type=client_credentials (example expires_in 5587808 s; FAQ: token active 60 days, max 25 active tokens per app). Calls: POST https://api.igdb.com/v4/{endpoint} with headers Client-ID and 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', Apicalypse body. Default limit 10, max 500 items/request; /v4/multiquery max 10 queries. Twitch account needs 2FA; app Client Type 'Confidential'. Docs: 'the API does not allow requests directly from browsers' -> backend proxy so secret/token never ship in a client. Official Node wrapper igdb-api-node 6.0.5 (2025-02-13). Not live-tested (needs credentials).

findings.topic: IGDB - licence, commercial use, caching, sync
findings.claim: IGDB is free for both non-commercial and commercial projects; commercial (monetized) use goes through a free partnership (partner@igdb.com) that asks for visible user-facing attribution (or, alternatively, sharing data with IGDB), and local storage/caching of IGDB data is explicitly preferred.
findings.details: [doc] 'free for non-commercial usage under the terms of the Twitch Developer Service Agreement'; FAQ: 'The API is free for both non-commercial and commercial projects'; partnership asks 'user facing attribution to IGDB.com' in 'a static location (e.g. not in a change log)'; 'Yes. In fact, we prefer if you store and serve the data to your end users'; data may be kept after partnership termination. Daily CSV dumps are 'exclusively available to our Data Partners'. Webhooks: POST /v4/{endpoint}/webhooks/ with url, secret, method=create|update|delete; deliveries carry X-Secret header; delete sends only the ID.

findings.claim: IGDB /v4/external_games links each IGDB game to store IDs through external_game_source + uid; Steam is source 1 with uid = the Steam appid as a string; other sources include GOG 5, Microsoft 11, Epic 26, Xbox Marketplace 31, PlayStation Store US 36.
findings.details: [doc] Fields: game, uid (String), external_game_source, platform, game_release_format, countries, url, name, year. 'category' and 'media' are DEPRECATED (enum-to-table migration, period 'February 18 to August 31', year not shown; enum values keep the same IDs). More sources: apple 13, android 15, itch_io 30, gamejolt 55. Lookup: POST /v4/external_games body 'fields game,uid; where external_game_source = 1 & uid = "1145360";'. [community] An undated Twitch dev-forum example filters /games with external_games.category & external_games.uid, so nested filtering works. Not live-tested (needs credentials).

findings.claim: IGDB exposes official time-to-beat data at /v4/game_time_to_beats with hastily, normally and completely (seconds) plus a submission count, a licensed replacement for HowLongToBeat.
findings.details: [doc] POST https://api.igdb.com/v4/game_time_to_beats; fields: game_id, hastily ('to its credits without spending notable time on extras such as side quests'), normally ('mixing in some extras such as side quests without being overly thorough'), completely ('to 100% completion'), count ('Total number of time to beat submissions'), created_at, updated_at, checksum. [inference] Coverage depends on community submissions, so niche games may have no or few data points; hide values when count is low. Maps naturally to 'completado' (normally) and 'platinado' (completely) estimates.

findings.topic: IGDB - work vs edition model and release status
findings.claim: IGDB distinguishes main games from DLC/editions/ports (game_type, version_parent, parent_game) and tracks game_status values including early_access, cancelled, rumored and delisted, plus per-platform/region release_dates.
findings.details: [doc] Legacy enum values (now tables game_types/game_statuses): main_game 0, dlc_addon 1, expansion 2, bundle 3, standalone_expansion 4, mod 5, episode 6, season 7, remake 8, remaster 9, expanded_game 10, port 11, fork 12, pack 13, update 14; status released 0, alpha 2, beta 3, early_access 4, offline 5, cancelled 6, rumored 7, delisted 8. Docs example: 'search "Assassins Creed"; where version_parent = null;' excludes editions. release_dates: date, human, platform, release_region, date_format (category/region deprecated). [inference] Lets GameAgenda collapse editions into one to-play item and accept upcoming/rumored games.

findings.claim: IGDB is the de-facto data source for backlog trackers (Backloggd: all its game data comes from IGDB) and held about 428,000 game entries, 196,500 of them DLCs/re-releases, as of March 2023.
findings.details: [secondary] Backloggd About: missing games are added on IGDB and pulled automatically after approval; directory listings say MyGamingBacklog, Gamestache and SavePoint also use IGDB. The 428k figure is Wikipedia 'as of March 2023'; today's count unverified (POST /v4/games/count with credentials). [live, Wikidata 2026-10-28] 152,541 items carry an IGDB ID; 116,986 of the 128,840 items with a Steam appid also have one (~91%), so IGDB-Steam overlap is high. Images: https://images.igdb.com/igdb/image/upload/t_{size}/{image_id}.jpg, cover_big 264x374, append _2x for retina.

findings.claim: RAWG requires an API key (live: HTTP 401 without it); the free tier gives 20,000 requests/month with a mandatory active backlink on every page that uses the data, its ToS bars further distribution, and there is no lookup by Steam appid.
findings.details: [live] GET https://api.rawg.io/api/games?search=hades without key -> 401 'The key parameter is not provided'. [doc] Business 50,000 req/month (apidocs shows '$149/m.', label placement ambiguous); Enterprise up to 1,000,000. ToS (last update 1 Mar 2021) 8.2.1: 'attribute RAWG as the source' and 'add an active hyperlink from every page where the data of RAWG is used'; free only with <=100,000 MAU or 500,000 page views/month; 4.3(5) 'not to use Services for the purposes of further distribution in any way'; 6.2 bars copying to another server without consent -> a local mirror is doubtful. OpenAPI v1.0 /games has no appid filter; /games/{id}/stores returns store URLs.

findings.claim: SteamGridDB API v2 (free personal Bearer key) fetches grids/heroes/logos/icons by Steam appid, but only supports platforms steam, origin, egs, bnet, uplay, flashpoint and eshop (no PlayStation/Xbox), and its Terms forbid automated use of the service.
findings.details: [doc] OpenAPI 2.10.0 (www.steamgriddb.com/static/openapi.yml): GET /games/{platform}/{platformId}, /grids/{platform}/{id*} (comma-separated ids), same for heroes/logos/icons, /search/autocomplete/{term}; limit default 50, 'Values > 50 will be ignored'; no rate limit documented. [live] /api/v2/games/steam/730 without key -> 401 'Authentication Required'. [community] Terms effective 2019-07-31, quoted in a 2026-10-11 GitHub PR, forbid 'any automated use of the Site, the Service'; art is user-uploaded and uploaders keep ownership. [inference] Steam already serves library_600x900 and hero assets, so SGDB adds little for Steam games.

findings.claim: The MobyGames API is no longer free: Hobbyist (non-commercial) is about $9.99/month and commercial use starts at Bronze, $99.99/month for 1 request/second (Silver $499.99 for 4 req/s, Gold $4,999.99 for 8 req/s).
findings.details: [secondary] Figures from the official subscribe page as indexed by search; direct fetch hit a Cloudflare 403 on 2026-10-28. A MobyPlus+Hobbyist bundle is listed at $12.99. A March 2025 forum announcement put Hobbyist at 0.2 req/s while the subscribe page shows 1 req/s (conflict unresolved). Free keys ended around Sept 2024 (third-party plugin docs and GitHub issue). Researchers and not-for-profits can apply for free access. [live, Wikidata] 77,042 MobyGames game-ID statements (P11688), often several per work (Hades: 122190, 252106, 177783).

findings.claim: The Giant Bomb API is currently unavailable: its /api page (live 2026-10-28) says that after going independent from Fandom the access mechanisms 'are not currently available, and they will change'.
findings.details: [live] giantbomb.com/api text: 'with the move to become independent from Fandom, we had to rebuild our tech stack completely from scratch. We DID bring all the wiki's data with us - but the mechanisms by which one could access them are not currently available'; lists Games, Characters, Companies, Concepts, Releases, People as not available; a MediaWiki rebuild is in 'rough, alpha state'. Footer: Copyright 2026 Jeffinitely LLC. [live, Wikidata] P5247 is now labelled 'Giant Bomb ID (former scheme)' and P14470 'Giant Bomb Wiki ID' has 68,873 statements. [community] Historic terms were non-commercial only.

findings.claim: HowLongToBeat has no official public API; unofficial clients reverse-engineer internal endpoints that keep moving (Aug 2025, Feb 2026, Oct 2026 '/api/bleed' to '/api/search/site') and HLTB has answered bursts with 429 since late September 2026.
findings.details: [community/source] dpashutskii/howlongtobeat PR #3 (2026-10-05/06): HLTB 'started answering 429 {"error":"Too many requests"} to bursts in late September 2026, on /api/search/site/init'; old client made ~8 requests per lookup. jasielrt95/hltb-client PR #2 (2026-10-18): '/api/bleed' replaced by '/api/search/site'; token no longer has hpKey/hpVal. ScrappyCocco PythonAPI (Aug 2025) reads the search endpoint from site JS. npm 'howlongtobeat' last release 1.8.0 (2023-07-09). HLTB ToS could not be retrieved (fetch blocked) -> unverified. Alternative: IGDB time-to-beat plus an outbound HLTB link via Wikidata P2816 (48,720 IDs).

findings.topic: IsThereAnyDeal API - access, limits, Steam lookup
findings.claim: The IsThereAnyDeal API requires a registered app key (the docs list no fees), is limited to 1000 requests per 5-minute window (verified email), and maps Steam appids to ITAD IDs; POST /lookup/id/shop/61/v1 answered without any key in a live test.
findings.details: [doc] Keys at isthereanydeal.com/apps/my/; key as ?key= or ITAD-API-Key header; OAuth2 code+PKCE for user data (/waitlist/games/v1, /collection/games/v1: GET/PUT/DELETE). 429 + Retry-After; 'Attempts to work around the limits will cause ban'. Prices: POST /games/prices/v3 (1-200 ITAD ids; country; shops e.g. 61=Steam, 35=GOG), /games/overview/v2 (best price + historical low), /games/historylow/v1, GET /games/lookup/v1?appid=. [live 2026-10-28] POST /lookup/id/shop/61/v1 ['app/1145360','app/730'] with no key -> 200 with ITAD UUIDs; GET /games/lookup/v1?appid=730 with no key -> 403 'Missing api key'.

findings.claim: ITAD's API terms allow commercial use only if the app is public, forbid changing provided data (affiliate tags, prices), and state 'You MUST NOT make an app that could be considered a competition to IsThereAnyDeal or IsThereAnyDeal projects'.
findings.details: [doc] Also: 'Private personal use is allowed. Private use beyond personal requires approval'; 'You SHOULD provide a link to IsThereAnyDeal.com or mention IsThereAnyDeal API'; 'You MUST NOT make an impression that you are affiliated with IsThereAnyDeal'; 'You MAY use only part of data provided and enrich them from your own sources'; 'We reserve the right to deny you access to the API at any point without notice.' [inference] ITAD runs its own Waitlist and Collection, so a to-play list plus 'comprado' tracker overlaps; showing ITAD prices for listed games is the intended use, but ask ITAD before a commercial launch and keep the price feature removable.

findings.claim: SteamSpy's keyless API still answers (live HTTP 200 for appid 730) but its data is stale and coarse: it returned the name 'Counter-Strike: Global Offensive', owners as the range '100,000,000 .. 200,000,000' and average_forever = 0.
findings.details: [live 2026-10-28] GET https://steamspy.com/api.php?request=appdetails&appid=730 -> 200, Cache-Control max-age=86400 (Cloudflare HIT); median_forever 0, ccu 1013936, tags with vote counts. [doc] 'Allowed poll rate - 1 request per second for most requests, 1 request per 60 seconds for the *all* requests' (all = 1,000 apps per page); 'The data is refreshed once a day'; appid 999999 means data hidden at the developer's request; no licence or terms stated. Use at most for tag/popularity hints, never as truth for names, playtime or ownership.

findings.claim: PlayStation trophy data is only reachable through unofficial reverse-engineered APIs (npm psn-api 2.18.1 of 2026-08-15; PSNAWP 3.1.0 of 2026-10-25) that authenticate with the user's NPSSO cookie, which conflicts with PSN Terms (revised March 2025) sections 10.7 and 5.1.
findings.details: [source] psn-api: read npsso at https://ca.account.sony.com/api/v1/ssocookie while signed in ('equivalent to your password') -> exchangeNpssoForAccessCode -> exchangeAccessCodeForAuthTokens -> exchangeRefreshTokenForAuthTokens; getUserTitles, getTitleTrophies, getUserTrophiesEarnedForTitle, getUserPlayedGames. [doc] PSN ToS 10.7: 'You may not use viruses, spyware, or automated methods, such as bots or scripts to interact with PSN Content'; 5.1: 'Do not phish for or harvest any accounts, account details, or other credentials.' [community] PSNAWP: 'Excessive use of API may lead to your PSN account being temporarily or permanently banned'; NPSSO lasts about 60 days.

findings.claim: OpenXBL (xbl.io) is a third-party Xbox Live REST API ('Not affiliated with Microsoft or Xbox') with a free tier of 150 requests/hour and paid tiers of $5 (500/h), $15 (2,500/h) and $35 (5,000/h) per month.
findings.details: [doc] Pricing page: Enterprise custom; 'Requests exceeding your OpenXBL rate limit will receive a 429 status code. Your limit resets every hour.'; all plans list 'Unlimited API keys & apps'. Auth header X-Authorization: <API key>; example GET /v2/player/gamertag/:gt; features achievements (unlock status, progression, rarity) and title history. [secondary] Its docs call it unofficial and its terms note Microsoft's own per-user throttling applies independently. No commercial-use clause on the pricing page. Suits an optional per-user Xbox achievement import, not a catalog.

findings.claim: The RetroAchievements Web API is free with a personal Web API key passed as y=, is rate-limited without published numbers, and has an official MIT client @retroachievements/api 2.10.0 (2026-02-04).
findings.details: [doc] Key from the account control panel; example https://retroachievements.org/API/API_GetTopTenUsers.php?y=KEY. 'Rate limiting is enabled', 'intended to provide a fair amount of burst requests to each user'; 'game data, tends to be very static' -> cache. Official clients: JS/TS (npm) and Kotlin. [secondary] Site terms: reproducing copyrighted works on their pages needs the rights holder's consent; no explicit commercial API clause found. [live, Wikidata] P11393 RetroAchievements game ID: 2,268 statements. Niche (emulated retro games): late, optional per-user import.

findings.claim: GOG publishes no official catalog API, but the undocumented catalog.gog.com/v1/catalog endpoint answered keyless in a live test, reporting 8,360 products (games+packs, ES/EUR) with id, slug, title, releaseDate, coverVertical, price and storeLink.
findings.details: [live 2026-10-28] GET https://catalog.gog.com/v1/catalog?limit=2&order=desc:trending&productType=in:game,pack&countryCode=ES&locale=es-ES&currencyCode=EUR -> 200; pages 4180; product keys include developers, publishers, operatingSystems, genres, tags, reviewsRating, editions. [community] gogapidocs.readthedocs.io calls itself unofficial documentation; a 2022 forum quote of a GOG partner page cites 200 requests/hour/IP on api.gog.com/products/*. No API terms grant found. Crosswalk via IGDB external_game_source 5 or Wikidata P2725 (4,927 statements). Optional enrichment only.

findings.claim: Epic offers no official public store-catalog API; the keyless freeGamesPromotions feed works (live: 13 elements for ES), while store.epicgames.com/graphql needs undocumented queries or persisted queries and is exposed to Cloudflare challenges.
findings.details: [live 2026-10-28] GET https://store-site-backend-static.ak.epicgames.com/freeGamesPromotions?locale=es-ES&country=ES&allowCountries=ES -> 200 (title, id, namespace, productSlug, offerType, keyImages, catalogNs.mappings, price, promotions). GET store.epicgames.com/graphql without a query -> 400 'GraphQL operations must contain a non-empty `query` or a `persistedQuery` extension.' [community] Oct 2026 issues report Cloudflare 403 challenges, notably for headless browsers. Crosswalk via IGDB external_game_source 26 or Wikidata P6278 (2,564 statements). Non-critical; do not scrape.

findings.claim: Wikidata structured data is CC0, and a live count on 2026-10-28 found: IGDB game ID (P5794) 153,661 statements, Steam application ID (P1733) 128,889, IsThereAnyDeal ID (P12570) 128,842, SteamGridDB ID (P12561) 125,923, MobyGames game ID (P11688) 77,042, RAWG game ID (P9968) 60,661, HowLongToBeat ID (P2816) 48,720.
findings.details: [live] Also: Giant Bomb Wiki ID P14470 68,873; PCGamingWiki P6337 42,366; Microsoft Store product ID P5885 6,851; PlayStation Store concept ID P12332 6,124; Nintendo eShop ID P8084 6,026; GOG application ID P2725 4,927; NA PS Store P5944 4,884; Epic Games Store ID P6278 2,564; RetroAchievements P11393 2,268; EU PS Store P5971 1,612. Distinct items: 128,840 with a Steam ID, of which 116,986 (~91%) also have IGDB and 40,693 (~32%) HLTB. [doc] Licensing page: structured data 'is released into the public domain under Creative Commons Zero'. Console-store coverage is thin.

findings.topic: Wikidata - crosswalk caveats and query limits
findings.claim: Wikidata external IDs are neither 1:1 nor always numeric: for Steam appid 1145360 (Hades, Q59756366) the IGDB ID is the slug 'hades--1', RAWG 'hades-2018', ITAD 'hades', and MobyGames has three values (122190, 252106, 177783).
findings.details: [live] Same item: HLTB 62941, SteamGridDB 4997889, PS Store concept 10002648, eShop 'hades-switch', Epic 'hades'. So store both IGDB numeric id and slug and allow several IDs per source. [doc] WDQS limits: 60 s query deadline; 60 s processing per 60 s per client (User-Agent+IP); 5 parallel queries per IP; 30 error queries/min; 429 with Retry-After; clients ignoring the User-Agent policy 'may be blocked completely'. Banner: the service 'is migrating to a new backend' in 2026-2027, which 'may require you to revise existing queries'. Use for batch enrichment, never in the typing path.

findings.claim: PCGamingWiki content is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), so its data, including Steam AppID infobox fields, is unsuitable for a product that may become commercial.
findings.details: [secondary] Wikipedia infobox lists 'Content licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0'; not verified on the wiki's own licence page. [live, Wikidata] 42,366 PCGamingWiki ID statements (P6337), so a link-out is possible without reusing content. [community] Other MediaWiki Cargo users advise not to call cargoquery in the critical path and to cache locally instead.

recommendations: Phase 1 (Steam only): keep Steam as the only catalog and source of truth; add no third-party catalog yet. Optional enrichments that do not slow capture: ITAD prices for 'quiero jugar/deseado' items (map appids with /lookup/id/shop/61/v1, then batch /games/prices/v3 with up to 200 ids, cache for hours), and later IGDB time-to-beat. Never use SteamSpy for user-facing names or playtime.

Phase 2 master catalog: use IGDB as the multi-platform catalog (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, GOG, Epic, retro). Mirror it into your own DB and local search index (IGDB prefers this), keep it fresh with webhooks (create/update/delete) plus periodic updated_at sweeps, and make every IGDB call from a backend (no CORS; never ship the Twitch client secret in a desktop/mobile/web client). If the app is ever monetized, email partner@igdb.com and add a static, visible 'Datos de juegos: IGDB.com' credit.

Join Steam and IGDB through IGDB external_games (external_game_source = 1, uid = appid). Keep Steam authoritative for Steam-specific fields (Spanish name/description, capsules, prices) and IGDB for everything else. Write code against the new IGDB field names (external_game_source, game_type, game_status, release_region), not the deprecated enums.

Use Wikidata (CC0) only as an offline/batch crosswalk to fill HLTB, ITAD, SteamGridDB, RAWG, MobyGames, PS Store and eShop IDs (for outbound links and de-duplication). Run it as scheduled jobs with a proper User-Agent, never on the search/typing path, and plan for the 2026-2027 WDQS backend migration.

Identity model: games(id UUID, canonical_title, normalized_title for search, kind main/dlc/edition/bundle, parent_game_id, release_status); game_external_ids(game_id, source enum steam|igdb|wikidata|itad|gog|epic|psn|xbox|nintendo|hltb|mobygames|rawg|sgdb|manual, external_id TEXT, id_kind numeric|slug|uuid, platform, region, url, match_method exact|crosswalk|fuzzy|user, confidence, verified_at, UNIQUE(source, external_id)); game_releases(game_id, platform, date, region); game_merges(old_id -> new_id) for later de-duplication. Allow several IDs per source (MobyGames-style) and store both IGDB numeric id and slug.

User state: user_entries(user_id, game_id, platform, want_to_play flag + priority, owned/'comprado' flag + store + date, completed date, platinum/100% date, abandoned, notes, timestamps). Keep these as independent flags/dates, not one status enum, because a game can be bought, completed and platinum at the same time.

Allow custom/manual games as first-class entries: saving with only a title (plus optional platform) must be instant and work offline; mark it 'unlinked' and let a background matcher suggest a Steam/IGDB match that the user confirms with one tap (never auto-link fuzzy matches such as 'Hades' vs 'Hades II'). This covers catalog gaps (console store IDs are sparse: about 6k PS Store or eShop IDs on Wikidata vs about 129k Steam), plus physical, retro, mobile, unannounced or rumored games.

Speed: put every third-party lookup behind your own cache and a per-source rate limiter (IGDB 4 rps and 8 concurrent; ITAD 1000 per 5 min; WDQS 5 parallel; SteamSpy 1 rps) with circuit breakers, so search and capture only ever hit the local index. Store raw payloads with fetched_at so you can re-map fields when providers deprecate them.

Achievements/'platinado': keep completed/platinum as manual toggles (the source of truth). Optional imports later: Steam (official Web API), Xbox via OpenXBL (user's own key or a paid tier), RetroAchievements (user key). For PSN either skip it or do a local-only import where the user's NPSSO never leaves their device, clearly labelled unofficial and at their own risk; never collect or store NPSSO tokens on a server.

Images and time: Steam assets for Steam games, IGDB covers (t_cover_big / t_cover_big_2x) for the rest; time-to-beat from IGDB game_time_to_beats, with HowLongToBeat only as an outbound link built from Wikidata P2816. SteamGridDB only as an opt-in, bring-your-own-key, personal-use feature.

Avoid for legal or stability reasons: scraping HowLongToBeat; the Giant Bomb API (offline); server-side PSN credential collection (PSN ToS 5.1/10.7); SteamGridDB for automated bulk or commercial use; RAWG as a mirrored/redistributed catalog or beyond its free tier without a contract; PCGamingWiki data (NC licence); MobyGames unless you pay; scraping Epic GraphQL; GOG/Epic unofficial endpoints for core features.
risks: Single-vendor dependency: the non-Steam catalog would rely on IGDB (Twitch/Amazon), whose terms, partnership policy or schema (the enum-to-table migration) can change; adapters and a local mirror reduce the impact.
Monetizing without an IGDB partnership and visible attribution would breach the IGDB/Twitch terms; RAWG commercial use above 100k MAU or 500k page views/month needs a contract.
ITAD can revoke access 'at any point without notice', and its 'no competition' clause could be read against a wishlist/collection tracker.
PSN auto-import exposes users to account bans and the app to ToS and credential-handling liability; NPSSO tokens are password-equivalent and expire about every 60 days (bad UX).

Unofficial endpoints (HLTB, GOG catalog, Epic GraphQL, PSN, OpenXBL upstream) break without notice: HLTB's internal API moved at least three times between Aug 2025 and Oct 2026 and started returning 429s.

Crosswalk errors: Wikidata IDs are multi-valued, slug-based and incomplete (console store IDs ~2.5k-7k), so treating them as 1:1 would cause wrong merges; fuzzy title matching can link the wrong game (sequels, remakes, editions).
WDQS backend migration (2026-2027) may break SPARQL queries; query limits (60 s, 5 parallel per IP) make it unsuitable for interactive use.
Image rights: SteamGridDB art is user-uploaded with unclear rights and terms that bar automated use; IGDB and Steam images remain the rights holders' property.
Stale data sources (SteamSpy, Giant Bomb former-scheme IDs) can show wrong names or broken links if used without validation.
open_questions: Will GameAgenda be public and/or monetized? This decides the IGDB partnership, the RAWG tier, SteamGridDB usability and ITAD's 'commercial if public' condition.
Is a small backend acceptable? It is required for IGDB (Twitch secret, no CORS) and for a shared catalog mirror; a purely local desktop app would need each user to create Twitch credentials.

Current IGDB size and per-platform crosswalk coverage were not measured (needs credentials): e.g. POST /v4/games/count and /v4/external_games/count where external_game_source = 36 (PlayStation) or 1 (Steam).
Has IGDB already removed the deprecated fields (category, media, region)? The docs still list them as deprecated on 2026-10-28; the year of the 'Feb 18 - Aug 31' migration is not shown.
Exact HowLongToBeat terms (not retrievable with the tools used) and current SteamGridDB terms text and rate limits (only quoted second-hand).
MobyGames Hobbyist rate (0.2 vs 1 req/s) and current prices: confirm on the live subscribe page if it is ever considered.
Does the user actually want automatic PSN/Xbox trophy import, given the ToS risk, or is a manual 'platinado' toggle enough?
Would ITAD consider a backlog/collection app 'competition'? Ask them before any commercial launch that shows their prices.

verdicts.evidence: Docs (undated): partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/auth says 'Steam is an OpenID Provider, as described in the OpenID 2.0 specification', with claimed ID 'http://steamcommunity.com/openid/id/<steamid>'. It labels https://steamcommunity.com/openid/ as the 'OP Endpoint URL'; that is really the discovery URL. Live 2026-10-28: the XRDS from /openid gives Type http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0/server and URI https://steamcommunity.com/openid/login. GET /.well-known/openid-configuration returns a 302 to the homepage, so there is no OIDC discovery document. OAuth doc: 'Valve will assign a Client ID', and none is given without cross-platform Cloud sync or Workshop. Scopes are read_cloud and write_cloud, token_type is steam, login is at steamcommunity.com/oauth/login. The Auth.js provider grid has no Steam provider (the S entries are Salesforce, Slack, Spotify, Strava).

Source code: DoctorMcKay/node-steam-signin index.js sends openid.ns=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0, mode=checkid_setup, claimed_id=identity=identifier_select, realm and return_to. It verifies with an HTTPS POST to steamcommunity.com/openid/login carrying openid.mode=check_authentication, assoc_handle, signed, sig and every field named in openid.signed, and accepts only a line 'is_valid:true'. Live 2026-10-28: a forged POST returned 200 text/plain 'ns:http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0\nis_valid:false'. A checkid_setup GET returned a 302 to /openid/loginform/?goto=..., which served 200 'Sign In'. The partner doc shows http:// claimed IDs and steamcommunity.com/dev shows https://. The steam-signin regex ^https?://steamcommunity\.com/openid/id/(\d+)/?$ accepts both. passport-steam needs an apiKey only for profile fetching (profile:false skips it).

CVE-2026-82183 was published to NVD on 2026-09-02 (the SentinelOne header says Sept 3). CVSS 3.1 is 8.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), CWE-287. Aggregators give the affected range as 6.25.0 to 7.0.0, fixed in 7.0.1. The plugin skipped re-posting to /openid/login with check_authentication. GHSA-hhw9-35p2-q2c5: published 2021-01-29, Critical, socialiteproviders/steam <1.1, 'allowing a malicious actor to substitute their own openID server'. Spec text checked: s11.1 says scheme, authority and path MUST match. s11.4.2.1 says 'To prevent replay attacks, the OP MUST NOT issue more than one verification response for each authentication response it had previously issued.' steam-signin requires claimed_id, return_to and response_nonce in openid.signed, hardcodes the host and regex-checks claimed_id. Caveat: steam-signin compares only the canonicalized realm of return_to, so matching the full return_to is extra hardening.

verdicts.correction: The approach is feasible in principle: OpenID 2.0 needs no secret, and the plugin and doc facts are right. The live 'acceptance' evidence is invalid, though. Steam's /openid/login also 302s to the normal 200 'Sign In' page for realm https://a.example with return_to gameagenda://auth/cb, a pair that breaks OpenID s9.2, so a pre-login 302/200 proves nothing. Whether Steam delivers the positive assertion to http://127.0.0.1:<port> or to a custom scheme stays unverified until a real end-to-end login. passport-steam's http://localhost:3000 example only suggests loopback works. A safer default is an HTTPS return_to on a server that verifies with check_authentication and then bounces to the deep link. Loopback should be tested as a variant.

verdicts.correction: The core holds. The doc says owned games come back 'if their owned games/game details are visible to you', a server key sees a stranger's view so Game details must be Public, and GetOwnedGames then answers 200 {"response":{}}. Three points need fixing. (1) communityvisibilitystate (1/3) and the XML privacyState describe PROFILE visibility, not Game details. A Public profile can still hide game details, so neither field detects this case; detect it from an empty GetOwnedGames reply (no game_count) on a public profile instead. (2) Not every endpoint answers 200 {}: key-based ISteamUserStats calls reportedly answer HTTP 403 'Profile is not public'. (3) Users can mark individual games Private, which hides them even when Game details is Public, so a 'comprado' import can be incomplete. A 'keep total playtime private' setting is also reported to break imports. Reports conflict on whether an account's own key can read its own private library.

verdicts.correction: The arithmetic and design advice hold as inference (about 300 calls per scan, about 330 scans/day; user-triggered, incremental, cached; queue plus backoff; never retry 401). Two parts are wrong. (1) The ToU caps 'calls to the Steam Web API' made by 'You', the licensee, at 100,000/day. It does not say 'per key' and does not exempt keyless calls, so all backend Steam Web API calls should be budgeted against it. (2) The cited Apr-Jun 2025 thread is about key-based calls (a profile-details request every 120 s gave a 429 every 10-20 min), not keyless endpoints. It does not establish a per-IP limit: one user still got 429s with a new IP and a fresh key, and others suspect shadow, global or time-of-day throttling. No Valve reply.
