'pages' seems to be computed for a fixed page size of about 50 rather than the requested limit, so paginate by productCount/limit, not by 'pages'. Wikidata P2725 had 5,058 statements in my all-statements count, versus 4,927 (depends on counting method). The '200 requests/hour/IP' figure stays unverified.
verdicts.evidence: Live 2026-10-28: GET catalog.gog.com/v1/catalog?limit=2&order=desc:trending&productType=in:game,pack&countryCode=ES&locale=es-ES&currencyCode=EUR returned 200 application/json. Body: pages 168, currentlyShownProductCount 8360, productCount 8360, 2 products. Product keys: id, slug, features, screenshots, releaseDate, storeReleaseDate, productType, title, coverHorizontal, coverVertical, logo, developers, publishers, operatingSystems, price, genres, tags, reviewsRating, editions, ratings, storeLink. Sample: Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition, 31,99 €. gogapidocs.readthedocs.io: 'Welcome to the unoffical documentation of the APIs used by the GOG website and Galaxy client'. It does not cover catalog.gog.com or rate limits.

Live 2026-10-28: freeGamesPromotions?locale=es-ES&country=ES&allowCountries=ES returned 200 with 13 elements. Element keys: title, id, namespace, description, effectiveDate, offerType, keyImages, seller, productSlug, urlSlug, items, categories, tags, catalogNs, offerMappings, price, promotions. My GET to store.epicgames.com/graphql with no query returned HTTP 403, a Cloudflare challenge page (challenge-platform), not the 400 GraphQL message the researchers saw. That supports exposure to Cloudflare challenges; results vary by client. No official public catalog API was found. My WDQS count: P6278 has 2,575 statements (2,564 claimed; depends on counting method).

Primary, live 2026-10-28: PCGamingWiki's own MediaWiki API (w/api.php?action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=rightsinfo) returns rightsinfo url '//creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0', text 'Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial Share Alike'. This upgrades the claim's secondary Wikipedia infobox source. Nuance: single facts such as AppIDs are not copyrightable. Bulk extraction can still touch EU sui generis database rights, which CC 3.0 unported does not license, so the conservative conclusion stands. My WDQS count: P6337 has 42,420 statements (42,366 claimed).

additional_findings.topic: CORS on keyless Steam store endpoints (PWA architecture)
additional_findings.claim: The keyless Steam endpoints used for game search and metadata, store.steampowered.com/api/storesearch and api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1, send no Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a third-party Origin. A PWA therefore cannot call any Steam data endpoint straight from the browser. Only CDN images are CORS-open.
additional_findings.details: Live 2026-10-28 with 'Origin: https://gameagenda.example'. storesearch/?term=portal&l=spanish&cc=ES: 200 JSON, no ACAO. IStoreBrowseService/GetItems (input_json appid 620): 200, no ACAO, 'Cache-Control: private, max-age=120'. OPTIONS preflight on api.steampowered.com: 405, so custom headers such as x-webapi-key never pass. For a PWA, the main 'search all Steam games' feature must use the app's own backend/edge proxy or a locally shipped, synced index. Tauri can call these from Rust. CDN images send ACAO *.

additional_findings.topic: Keyless Steam wishlist import for the 'quiero jugar' list
additional_findings.claim: IWishlistService/GetWishlist/v1 works with only a steamid and no key. It returns the whole Steam wishlist as items[{appid, priority, date_added}], which allows a one-click import into the main 'want to play' list.
additional_findings.details: Live 2026-10-28, public profile 76561197972494985: 200 with 47 items, e.g. {appid:311810, priority:24, date_added:1640445747}; GetWishlistItemCount gave {count:47}. xPaw lists both with steamid only. No names are returned, so join appids with the local catalog or GetItems. Responses are no-store with no ACAO, so a backend or Tauri is needed. Visibility follows the 2018 Game-details setting (untested on a private profile). Contrast: GetOwnedGames ('comprado') needs a key, so a backend-less Tauri app can import wishlist and achievements but not owned games.

additional_findings.topic: Steam OpenID pre-login responses prove nothing about realm/return_to acceptance
additional_findings.claim: Steam's /openid/login does not reject an invalid realm/return_to pair before login. Realm https://a.example with return_to gameagenda://auth/cb, which violates OpenID 2.0 s9.2, still 302s to /openid/loginform/ and renders the normal 200 'Sign In' page.
additional_findings.details: Live control test 2026-10-28. The page contained no realm error, only a hidden 2FA template string. So the earlier 'accepted loopback/custom scheme' tests (R3-05) are not evidence; any validation happens after credentials. Before fixing the Tauri auth design, run one real end-to-end login each for return_to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/cb and for an HTTPS return_to with a deep-link bounce, and note how Steam shows the site name. Until then the server-verified HTTPS bounce is the safer default.

additional_findings.topic: Per-game private titles make Steam library imports incomplete
additional_findings.claim: Steam lets users mark individual games Private. This hides those titles' ownership, playtime and activity from others even when Game details is Public, so a 'comprado' or achievement import through the Web API can be silently incomplete.
additional_findings.details: [secondary] The Steam Support 'Steam Private Games' FAQ (JS-rendered; content via search summary) says private games disappear from the public games list, recently played and 'Friends who own this'. The feature was first spotted Nov 2023 and later rolled out. [community] barryjj PR #220 (merged 2026-09-23): key-based stats endpoints answer 403 'Profile is not public' for a game marked private, and 'see the profile the way a stranger does'. Plan: treat Steam import as best-effort and keep manual add one keystroke away.

researches.label: product & UX benchmark
researches.summary:
I benchmarked 15+ trackers: Backloggd, HowLongToBeat, Playnite, LaunchBox, GameTrack, Stash, GG, IGN Playlist, Infinite Backlog, Completionator, Grouvee and Steam, plus newer 2025-26 apps (Playlogged, Tier, MyBacklog, Backlog VGO). They converge on about 5 exclusive progress states: want/backlog, playing, paused/on hold/shelved, beaten/completed, abandoned/dropped/quit. On top of that sits a separate top tier: Mastered, 100%, Completionist or Platinum. The better models keep the milestone and ownership on their own axes. Backloggd splits game toggles, a played sub-status, a 'Mastered' field and an 'Ownership' field. Infinite Backlog and Completionator store ownership details. Steam keeps wishlist, library and achievements apart. Many mobile apps instead mix Wishlist (want to buy) and Backlog (own it) into one status list.

Recommended model:
- Estado, one value: Quiero jugar (default), Jugando, En pausa, Completado or Abandonado.
- One-tap flags: Platinado, Comprado, Próximo, plus a Nota.
- 'Por comprar' and 'Pendientes que tengo' are derived filters.
- Platinado implies Completado. Dates are stamped automatically. Nothing asks for confirmation; an undo toast replaces dialogs.
- 'Completed' is ambiguous: on 2026-10-15 Steam renamed its 'Perfect Games' tab to 'Completed' (all achievements), while Backloggd uses it for beating the main objective. The app must define its labels.

Speed (tested live):
- Steam's keyless search took 259-384 ms per query and returned soundtracks and DLC.
- A local scan over 200k titles took about 5 ms median (p95 under 8 ms) in Node 24.
- So an instant omnibox (Ctrl+K or '/', Enter adds as Quiero jugar) needs a local, games-only, normalized index.
- Budgets: 50 ms per keystroke at p95, 100 ms tap feedback, INP p75 ≤200 ms, LCP ≤2.5 s, repeat start ≤2 s, no skeleton screens under 1 s.

Capture:
- MVP: paste any Steam link (store/app/ID, s.team/a/ID, which redirects there) or a bare appid.
- Web Share Target only works in installed PWAs on Chromium (Chrome Android 76+, desktop 89+). Safari/iOS and Firefox do not support it, so iPhone needs a Shortcut or a native share extension.
- Steam store pages block fetches to other origins (CSP connect-src) and block iframes (X-Frame-Options DENY). A bookmarklet must open /add?appid= instead of fetching.

Gaps and positioning: Backloggd's top unshipped requests are a native Android app (20K votes), Steam import (20K) and an iOS app (15K). Complaints center on entry friction, search ranking, slow loads, sync gaps and ads or paywalls. Compete on speed, Steam data in Spanish, Próximo plus notes, and the clean model. Leave discovery and price alerts to Steam. PSN auto-detection uses fragile unofficial APIs, so Platinado is manual in the MVP.

findings.claim: Backloggd tracks state on separate axes: per-game toggles (Played, Playing, Backlog, Wishlist), a per-log 'played' sub-status (Played, Completed, Retired, Shelved, Abandoned), a separate 'Mastered' field, and Library entries / an 'Ownership' field for ownership.
findings.details: About page: 'Played, Playing, Backlog, and Wishlist toggles for each game' plus 'Played, Completed, Abandoned, Retired, and Shelved options for the Played log status'. UI tooltips: Completed = 'Beat your main objective'; Retired = 'Finished with a game that lacks an ending'; Shelved = 'Unfinished but may pick up again later'; Abandoned = 'Unfinished and staying that way'. v1.14.0 (2025-04-24) added 'time to finish'/'time to master' and renamed the log 'Medium' field to 'Ownership'. v1.17.0 (2026-04-10) put Replay next to the 'Mastered' field. Game data comes from IGDB, so a missing game must first be added on IGDB.

findings.topic: Benchmark: unmet demand at the market leader
findings.claim: Backloggd's public roadmap (read 2026-10-28) shows its most-voted requests still unshipped: Android app 20K votes, Steam import 20K, iOS app 15K, CSV export 7.4K, CSV import 2.1K, mobile-browser improvements 1.6K.
findings.details: Roadmap items are open votes; none is marked shipped. Backloggd is web-only (fan-made wrappers exist). A report written by a competitor (Two Average Gamers/SavePoint, updated 2026-09-16) says users grew from about 350K to 650K+ during 2025 under a solo developer. The same report says users 'log many games in the first week, then gradually stop' (Backloggd, GG, spreadsheets). Takeaway: mobile capture that feels native, Steam-based data and export are proven unmet needs, and low-friction logging is what keeps people using it.

findings.claim: HowLongToBeat's user lists are Playing, Backlog, Replay, Custom, Completed and Retired (seen live in game-page data). It represents 100% only as a time category ('Completionist'), not as a status.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: howlongtobeat.com/game/10270 (The Witcher 3) embeds count_playing=558, count_backlog=33242, count_replay=2506, count_custom=1294, count_comp=27211, count_retired=1863. Labels: 'Playing', 'Backlogs', 'Replays', 'Retired', 'Beat'. Time categories: 'Main Story', 'Main + Sides', 'Completionist'. The page data also holds profile_steam=292030 (Steam appid) and the alias 'The Witcher III: Wild Hunt'. Reviews describe HLTB as ad-funded, with a free Steam import and a dated UI. I found no official public API, so integrating HLTB is a later, risky item.

findings.claim: Playnite seeds a new database with 8 user-editable completion statuses: 'Not Played', 'Played', 'Beaten', 'Completed', 'Playing', 'Abandoned', 'On Hold', 'Plan to Play'. It sets 'Not Played' on newly imported games and 'Played' on first play automatically.
findings.details: Source: GameDatabase.OpenDatabase() on master. defStatuses holds those 8 names; CompletionStatusSettings sets DefaultStatus = 'Not Played' and PlayedStatus = 'Played'; ImportGames() applies them. The manual's Library Manager exposes 'Default status assigned to newly added games' and 'Status assigned to games played for the first time'. Favorite and Hidden are separate booleans; user score, notes, tags and categories are separate fields. Lesson: one exclusive progress field, independent flags and automatic transitions. Playnite says its codebase is being rewritten for Playnite 11.

findings.claim: LaunchBox (13.22+) replaced its single 'Completed' checkbox with one exclusive Game Progress value grouped as Category/Value. The groups are Not Started (Unplayed, Want to Play, Won't Play), Active (In Progress, Continuous, Paused) and Done (Beaten, Completed, Mastered, Dropped), and automation rules set the value.
findings.details: Users can add, remove and reorder values (Tools > Options > Data > Game Progress Priorities); values in use can't be renamed or deleted. Default rules (the last match wins): no match → Unplayed; playtime > N min → In Progress; at least one achievement → In Progress; RetroAchievements beaten → Beaten; all RA softcore → Completed; all achievements incl. RA hardcore → Mastered. Achievement sources: Steam, GOG, RA. Games that were 'Completed' migrated to Done / Mastered. A feature request on the same board notes users misuse 'Completed' to mean 'tried it, won't return'.

findings.claim: GameTrack (iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS; 4.5 stars from 1.3K ratings) sorts games into lists, not a status field. It has the widest quick-add set: a share extension for Steam, PlayStation Store and Xbox links, barcode scanning (one game or a batch), Siri/Shortcuts and widgets.
findings.details: Lists: Backlog (Now Playing, Play Next, Collection), Archive (Finished, Completed, Abandoned), and a Wish List sorted by release date with release alerts; plus completion % and notes. These list names come from a MacStories review dated around Aug 2020 (date inferred). The current App Store page adds account linking (PlayStation, Xbox, Steam, Epic, GOG, RetroAchievements) including trophies, Steam import by Steam ID, and CSV import/export. Review complaints: sync gaps between devices ('does not sync to my iPad') and a PSN import that pulled '91 games' of about 1000. GameTrack+ costs $3.99/mo, $29.99/yr or $99.99 lifetime.

findings.claim: Mobile-first and 2025-2026 trackers converge on 4-6 exclusive states plus a wishlist; only outliers go further.
findings.details: Stash: Want, Playing, Beaten, Archived (4.7 stars, 585 ratings). IGN Playlist: Wishlist, Backlog, Playing, Paused, Beat, Quit, plus HLTB times. Playlogged (v1.0 on 12 Mar, probably 2026): Backlog, Playing, Completed, Dropped, Wishlist, Paused; swipe to change status, offline-first, a 'Next to Play' picker. Tier (vendor page, 2026-10-22): To play, Playing, Played, Abandoned, Replaying, 100% completed, plus a wishlist. Backlog VGO: Wishlist, Backlogged, Playing, Completed, Dropped; 'Pick a game's status right where you add it'. GG renamed 'Beaten' to 'Played' (v1.7.0) and added Wishlist and Backlog (v1.10.0). Outlier: MyBacklog has 10 statuses, incl. Replayed and Endless.

findings.claim: Only a minority of trackers model ownership separately from play status. The ones that do (Backloggd, Infinite Backlog, Completionator, Steam) treat it as a property with a source or format. Most mobile apps fold Wishlist (want to buy) and Backlog (own, unplayed) into the status list.
findings.details: Infinite Backlog tracks acquisition date and source, physical vs subscription, and lending. It imports Steam/GOG/PlayStation/Xbox with a review step for each game (Achriom 2026-09-01, written by a competitor). Play sessions are tagged played/beaten/completed/dropped/shelved (release 1.10). Completionator records 'what games you own, what platform they're on, what condition they're in', plus completion times and a Steam import. Backloggd renamed 'Medium' to 'Ownership' (v1.14). Steam keeps the wishlist separate from the library. Takeaway: make 'Comprado' a flag, and make wishlist vs backlog filters, not states.

findings.claim: 'Completed' means different things in different places. Backloggd uses it for beating the main objective. Steam's Achievement Sets beta (2026-10-15) renamed the 'Perfect Games' tab to 'Completed', meaning all achievements. RetroAchievements and LaunchBox rank Beaten < Completed < Mastered.
findings.details: Valve, 2026-10-15: 'The Perfect Games tab is now called Completed and expands to show both completed games and games with completed achievement sets'. Base-game and DLC achievements are separate sets; DLC achievements count only once the DLC is owned. A 'set complete' trophy survives later additions, and archived achievements don't block completion. PlayStation's Platinum requires all other base-game trophies (DLC is usually excluded, with exceptions, per Giant Bomb). Keep the user's words but define them in the app: Completado = main story or objective; Platinado (100%) = the platinum trophy or all base-game achievements.

findings.claim: Steam's own tools now cover 'want to buy' and discovery, but not 'want to play' progress across platforms. Wishlist custom categories went live 2026-07-22/23, and the Personal Calendar left Steam Labs on 2026-10-23.
findings.details: Wishlist (Game Developer, 2026-07-23): categories the user creates (e.g. 'buy when on sale', 'wait for reviews'), notifications limited to chosen categories (sale, Early Access→1.0, demo), shareable filtered views, search autocomplete, a demo label. Personal Calendar (Valve, 2026-10-23): algorithmic recent and upcoming games over an 8-week window, retrained daily, with filters for wishlisted, Early Access and DLC; in Labs since Oct 2025. Play Next (2020) suggests unplayed owned games. Takeaway: don't compete on discovery or price alerts; win on speed, a multi-platform list, progress states and notes.

findings.topic: What users praise and complain about
findings.claim: Complaints about trackers center on friction when adding games and the burden of data entry. Common ones: too many fields per update, many taps to rate, entering a platform for each game, poor search ranking and duplicate editions, slow loads, having to refresh after adding, sync gaps and paywalls.
findings.details: A 2024-01-01 blog says Infinite Backlog updates feel 'too much like homework', while GG's minimal logging 'encouraged quick, frequent entries'; it calls Backloggd's library details 'tedious'. App Store reviews: IGN Playlist takes 'several taps just to rate' and needs a platform for each game. GG gets 'lame loading times', 'the game I search for is often far down the list', having to 'refresh once after adding', and criticism of its $4.99/mo tier. GameTrack has sync gaps; Stash had a bug that reset ratings. Praise: 'Find the game..., click wishlist, and it's added. Simple.' Reddit was blocked, so this evidence leans on store reviews and blogs.

findings.topic: Recommended taxonomy: dimensions and Spanish labels
findings.claim: Recommended model: one exclusive 'Estado' with 5 values, three independent one-tap flags (Platinado, Comprado, Próximo) and an optional free-text Nota. Wishlist and backlog become filters.
findings.details: Estado (exactly one): Quiero jugar (default when added), Jugando, En pausa, Completado, Abandonado. Flags: Platinado (100%); Comprado, with an optional 'dónde' (Steam, PlayStation, Físico, Suscripción, Regalo); Próximo (a pin, or manual order inside Quiero jugar). Derived views: Por comprar = Quiero jugar and not Comprado; Pendientes que tengo = Quiero jugar and Comprado; Platinados. This matches the common 5-state core (Playnite, LaunchBox, IGN Playlist, Playlogged) and keeps milestone and ownership on separate axes, as Backloggd and Steam do. Rating, dates and platform go in a secondary panel.

findings.claim: State changes should happen automatically and be undoable. Setting Platinado also sets Completado, entering a state stamps its date, and no change asks for confirmation or extra fields.
findings.details:
Rules:
- Adding a game sets Quiero jugar (addedAt).
- Jugando sets startedAt if empty; Jugando ↔ En pausa.
- Abandonado sets droppedAt; the game can come back.
- Completado sets completedAt, kept on replay (Completado → Jugando = 'Rejugando', count +1).
- Platinado ON also sets Completado (+completedAt) if needed, as one undoable action; OFF leaves Estado alone.
- Comprado never changes Estado (subscription and free-to-play games exist).
- Delete is immediate, with undo. Dates can be edited later.
This mirrors Playnite's automatic statuses and LaunchBox's rules, and avoids the 'homework' complaint.

findings.topic: Instant search needs a local index (live test)
findings.claim: Remote typeahead cannot feel instant. Steam's keyless store search took 259-384 ms per query in live tests. An in-memory substring scan over 200,000 titles took about 4-6 ms median (p95 under 8 ms) in Node 24 on this machine.
findings.details:
Live 2026-10-28:
- storesearch/?term=hollow%20knight&l=spanish&cc=ES → 200, 1,967 B, 0.384 s total (TLS done at 0.133 s).
- /search/suggest?term=hollow%20knight&f=games → 0.259 s.
Single samples; they depend on the network. Both returned soundtracks and DLC, and storesearch typed all 5 items as 'app'. Benchmark: 200k synthetic names, a one-time 73 ms normalization pass, about 31 MB heap. 12 queries × 20 runs gave a median of 3.6-5.8 ms and a p95 of 4.8-7.6 ms. Phones may be several times slower (inference) but should stay under 50 ms; run the search in a Web Worker.

findings.claim: Budgets backed by published standards: 50 ms from keystroke to results (p95), 100 ms from tap to feedback, INP ≤200 ms at p75, first-visit LCP ≤2.5 s at p75, cached restart ≤2 s, no spinner or skeleton for waits under a second, and a native cold start well below Android's 5 s 'excessive' threshold.
findings.details: RAIL (web.dev, 2020-06-10): handle input within 50 ms, show a response within 100 ms, ≤10 ms of work per frame, first load interactive ≤5 s on mid-range mobile over slow 3G, repeat loads <2 s. Nielsen: 0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps flow, 10 s keeps attention. INP: good ≤200 ms, poor >500 ms. LCP: good ≤2.5 s, poor >4 s (both p75; updated Sep 2025). NN/g: waits under 1 s need no skeleton or spinner. Android vitals 'excessive' time to first frame: cold ≥5 s, warm ≥2 s, hot ≥1.5 s (2026-09-21). Superhuman: '100ms rule' (2022). Suggested target: ≤1.5 s to first frame.

findings.topic: Optimistic local-first writes and undo instead of confirmations
findings.claim: Save changes locally and show them immediately, then offer an undo toast instead of confirmation dialogs. NN/g and Raskin show people click through confirmations out of habit, and a local-first store removes network waits from every interaction.
findings.details: NN/g (2018-02-18, reviewed 2026-08-07): warn too often and 'they stop paying attention'; users 'click Yes without thinking'; 'go to great lengths to provide undo'. Raskin (A List Apart, 2007-07-21): 'Never use a warning when you mean undo'. Ink & Switch local-first essay (Apr 2019), ideal 'No spinners': the primary copy lives on the device, reads and writes are local, and sync runs in the background. Practice: write to IndexedDB/SQLite first, render in the same frame, show 'Añadido a Quiero jugar · Deshacer' for about 5-8 s, support Ctrl+Z, sync later.

findings.claim: A PWA can receive 'Share → GameAgenda' from the Steam app only on Chromium browsers (Chrome Android 76+, desktop Chrome 89+, Edge, Opera). Safari (macOS and iOS) and Firefox do not support Web Share Target, and the app must be installed.
findings.details: MDN browser-compat-data (fetched 2026-10-28): chrome 89, chrome_android 76, opera 76, opera_android 63. Edge and Samsung Internet follow Chromium. firefox: false; firefox_android 'parses, but has no effect'; safari: false, and safari_ios follows safari. The feature is experimental. MDN (modified 2026-08-27) says it only works once the PWA is installed. Chrome docs: on Android the url field is often empty and the link arrives in text, so parse every field. iPhone fallbacks: detect pasted links, an iOS Shortcut that opens /add?url=, or a native share extension (GameTrack ships one).

findings.topic: Capturing from Steam links and pages (live test)
findings.claim: Adding from Steam means parsing several link forms and working within Steam's page security. s.team/a/<appid> redirects (302) to store.steampowered.com/app/<appid>/. Store pages send a CSP whose connect-src allows only Valve domains, plus X-Frame-Options: DENY.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28: https://s.team/a/730 → 302 to https://store.steampowered.com/app/730/. The store page CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' in script-src, so bookmarklets run. But connect-src allows only Steam/Valve hosts, so a bookmarklet can't fetch() your API; it should open https://<app>/add?appid=730 instead. X-Frame-Options: DENY blocks iframes. Chrome docs: content scripts act with the page's origin, so network calls go through the extension's service worker. The parser should accept store.steampowered.com/app/<id>[/slug], s.team/a/<id> and a bare appid; steamcommunity.com/app/<id> is likely too (inference).

findings.topic: Precedent: add buttons on Steam store pages
findings.claim: Adding a button to Steam store pages is a proven pattern. The Backloggd Plus userscript adds Steam/SteamDB → Backloggd buttons, the Steam HLTB add-on adds a button next to 'Community Hub', and Augmented Steam highlights owned or wishlisted games and keeps notes per game.
findings.details: Backloggd Plus (Greasy Fork, 'early' v0.7.21) puts its button in .apphub_OtherSiteInfo, styled like the SteamDB / Community Hub links, and offers es/es-419 UI. Augmented Steam (IsThereAnyDeal; v4.2.1, Dec 2024; some reviews say it 'stopped working') also shows HLTB times and price history. Idea for a later phase: a '+ Quiero jugar' button and a 'Ya en tu agenda: Jugando' badge. Steam page changes break injected buttons, so keep the extension minimal: read the appid from the URL and hand off to the app.

findings.topic: Omnibox / command palette and keyboard flow
findings.claim: The fastest way to add a game is one search box that is always available (Ctrl+K or '/') and works as both search and command line. It needs fuzzy, alias-aware, ranked results and full keyboard navigation per the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern; Enter adds the highlighted game as 'Quiero jugar'.
findings.details: Superhuman (2021-10-12): 'one shortcut rules them all: Cmd+K', the same key closes it, fuzzy matching ('opn' → Open), aliases, score-based ranking, reordering by usage. WAI-ARIA combobox: Down/Up move into the list, Enter accepts, Escape closes, focus stays in the input via aria-activedescendant, plus aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-autocomplete=list. Things' Quick Entry opens from any app with Ctrl+Space; Tauri's global-shortcut plugin (desktop only, Rust ≥1.90) allows the same. Keys: Enter = Quiero jugar, Shift+Enter = Jugando, Ctrl+Enter = add with a note, 1-5 = Estado, C = Comprado, P = Platinado, Ctrl+Z = undo.

findings.topic: Search quality rules for Steam titles
findings.claim: Search quality matters as much as speed for quick adding. Steam names carry ®/™ symbols, numeral variants and many non-game items, so the index must normalize names, support aliases and show only games by default.
findings.details:
Seen in this research: titles like 'Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4' and 'LEGO® Batman™: Legacy of the Dark Knight' (Valve post); HLTB keeps the alias 'The Witcher III: Wild Hunt'; Steam search for 'hollow knight' returned soundtracks. GG reviews say the right game is 'often far down the list' and complain about duplicate editions. Rules:
- Ignore case and accents; strip ®™© and punctuation.
- Map Roman and Arabic numerals; match word prefixes ('dark sou').
- Rank exact > prefix > substring, break ties by popularity.
- Hide DLC, soundtracks, demos and tools by default (needs a type field in the index).
- Always offer 'Añadir «…» como juego propio'.

findings.claim: Steam's small capsule images are about 3.6× lighter than header images and are cached long-term by the CDN. List rows should use capsule_231x87 with native lazy-loading and fixed dimensions, inside a virtualized list.
findings.details: Live 2026-10-28, shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/730/: capsule_231x87.jpg 9,528 B; header.jpg 34,296 B; library_600x900.jpg 38,081 B; Cache-Control public, max-age ≈3.1e8 s (about 10 years). 50 rows ≈ 0.48 MB, vs ≈ 1.7 MB with headers. web.dev: loading='lazy' works in Chrome 77, Edge 79, Firefox 75 and Safari 15.4; don't lazy-load the LCP image; set width/height to avoid layout shift; virtualize long lists. Caveat: GetItems returns hashed asset paths; the unhashed paths worked for appid 730 but need checking for newer apps.

findings.claim: Detecting PlayStation platinums automatically depends on unofficial APIs, so in the MVP Platinado should be a manual one-tap flag.
findings.details: psn-api (a JS wrapper) states it 'is not affiliated with Sony or PlayStation' and that such wrappers are 'notorious for breaking when Sony changes something'. Login means signing in on playstation.com, copying an NPSSO token from ca.account.sony.com/api/v1/ssocookie, and renewing it about every two months. GameTrack and MyBacklog do offer PSN import, with reported gaps (91 of about 1000 games). Detecting 100% on Steam is possible later through the official Web API (key plus a public profile; covered by another research area). It must follow the new Achievement Sets rules, which separate base-game and DLC achievements.

findings.claim: MVP: instant capture, the 5 Estados and 3 flags, local-first storage and a Spanish UI. Accounts and sync, imports, share targets and extensions, social features and stats come later.
findings.details:
Must-have:
- A local index of Steam games with typeahead under 50 ms, and a search box that accepts names, Steam URLs (store/app, s.team/a) and appids. Enter = Quiero jugar.
- Custom entries for non-Steam games.
- Estado, Platinado/Comprado/Próximo and Nota; tabs with counts, filters (Por comprar, Platinados), sorting (añadido, próximo, nombre).
- Shortcuts, instant local saves with undo, offline storage, JSON/CSV export and import (Backloggd's export request has 7.4K votes).
Next: sync between devices, share targets, a Steam-page button or bookmarklet, Steam library import, release reminders. Later or maybe: PSN, automatic achievement detection, HLTB times, ratings, social.

findings.claim: Differentiators that hold up against Backloggd, HLTB and GG: speed as the product itself, a Steam-based catalog with Spanish metadata, notebook-style 'Próximo' plus notes, a clean model where Comprado and Platinado are separate flags, no ads and no account needed to start, and a Spanish-first UI.
findings.details: Gaps: Backloggd has no native app, no Steam import, and its catalog depends on IGDB. HLTB is ad-funded with a dated UI. GG's paywall and loading times draw complaints. Steam covers only 'want to buy' and discovery. appdetails accepts l=spanish (confirmed in the given live probes), so Spanish descriptions are available. I found no official Spanish UI for Backloggd (only a third-party userscript); Tier says it supports 8 languages. Risk: Steam-only users may find Steam's wishlist categories good enough, so lead with speed, a multi-platform list, the Estados and notes.

recommendations: Use one exclusive Estado (Quiero jugar default, Jugando, En pausa, Completado, Abandonado) plus three one-tap flags (Platinado, Comprado, Próximo) and an optional Nota. Make 'Por comprar' and 'Pendientes que tengo' filters, not states.
Show what each label means in the app: Completado = main story or objective finished; Platinado (100%) = platinum trophy or all base-game achievements. Steam now uses 'Completed' to mean 100%.
Make Platinado set Completado in the same undoable action. Stamp addedAt, startedAt, completedAt, droppedAt and platinumAt automatically, and never require extra fields to change state.

Make the search box the main screen: focused on open, reachable with Ctrl+K or '/', full keyboard navigation (WAI-ARIA combobox), and Enter adds the highlighted game as Quiero jugar. Offer 'Añadir «…» como juego propio' when nothing matches.

Ship a local, games-only Steam index (no DLC, soundtracks, demos or tools by default). Ignore case and accents, strip ®™, and map Roman and Arabic numerals. Run the search in a Web Worker and use remote Steam search only as a fallback.

Set performance budgets and test them on a mid-range Android phone: keystroke to results ≤50 ms (p95), tap to feedback ≤100 ms, INP p75 ≤200 ms (aim for 100), first-visit LCP ≤2.5 s, cached restart ≤2 s, no skeleton or spinner for sub-second operations.
Save locally first and render immediately. Replace every confirmation dialog, including delete, with an undo toast (about 5-8 s) and Ctrl+Z.

Include Steam link parsing in the MVP: store.steampowered.com/app/<id>, s.team/a/<id> and a bare appid, pasted into the search box. Add the Android share target (installed PWA) next, and handle iOS with a Shortcut or a native share extension.

For a bookmarklet or browser extension, open https://<app>/add?appid=<id> instead of calling fetch(), because Steam's CSP connect-src blocks other origins. In an extension, make network calls from the service worker and keep the content script minimal.
Use capsule_231x87 thumbnails (~9.5 KB) with loading='lazy' and fixed width/height in a virtualized list. Use header or library art only in the detail view.
Offer JSON/CSV export and import from day one as a backup and to avoid lock-in.

Leave discovery, price alerts and social features to Steam and Backloggd. Keep Platinado manual in the MVP; consider Steam achievement detection later and PSN import last, since its APIs are unofficial and break.
risks: Download size and parse time of the local catalog index can hurt cold start. The real Steam catalog size, compressed payload and update strategy must come from the data research area; my benchmark used 200k synthetic names.
Steam endpoints change: ISteamApps/GetAppList v2 is gone (ground truth), and keyless store endpoints may change or rate-limit, which affects both the catalog pipeline and the fallback search.
Label confusion: Steam now calls 100% achievements 'Completed', and PlayStation Platinum usually excludes DLC trophies. Without clear definitions, users will misread 'Completado' and 'Platinado'.
iPhone PWAs cannot be share targets (Safari does not support Web Share Target). If the user mainly captures on iOS, a native wrapper or share extension moves up in priority.
Without popularity data, search ranking may bury the intended game; this was a recurring GG complaint. A ranking signal has to come from data research.
Steam page markup changes can break an injected button, and the CSP blocks fetches from bookmarklets to other origins.
PSN import and trophy detection depend on unofficial wrappers that need a manually renewed NPSSO token, so they are fragile and may conflict with terms of service.
Engagement drops after the first week (reported across trackers): any extra friction when adding games, such as forms, required fields or confirmations, will kill continued use.
Scope creep toward social features, reviews or discovery puts the app up against Backloggd and Steam's own features without an advantage.
Complaint evidence leans on App Store reviews and blogs, some written by competitors (Achriom, SavePoint/TAG, Tier). Reddit could not be sampled because fetching was blocked.
open_questions: Where will the user mostly add games: on the PC (browser or Steam client) or on the phone (Android or iPhone)? This decides PWA vs a desktop or mobile wrapper and how urgent share targets are.
Is local-only storage acceptable for the MVP, or does the user need sync between devices (and so an account) from day one?
Should Platinado be one generic label ('Platinado (100%)'), or change per platform (Platino on PlayStation, 100% achievements on Steam, Completado on Xbox)?
Should DLC and expansions be trackable as their own entries, or only base games?
Is a yes/no 'Comprado' enough, or does the user want store or format details (Steam, PlayStation, físico, PS Plus, Game Pass, regalo)?
Are ratings, dates and playtime wanted in the MVP, or only state, flags and a note?
Should unreleased games in Quiero jugar get release-date reminders, given Steam's own wishlist and Personal Calendar already cover Steam titles?
How many games will a typical list hold (dozens or thousands)? This sets how much list virtualization and filtering the MVP needs.
Which platforms come after Steam (PlayStation, Switch, Xbox), and is a custom game entry acceptable for them in the meantime?

researches.label: 2026 tech stack
researches.summary:
The biggest factor in making the app fast ('rápida y ágil') is to run search and writes on the device. Live data (2026-10-28): the Steam games list has 196,595 entries with an average name length of 16.7 chars. A compact appid<TAB>name snapshot is 4.95 MiB raw, 2.44 MiB gzip and 1.80 MiB brotli. On this PC (Node 24.21), accent-folding every name takes 142 ms. A brute-force substring scan takes 6-9 ms per query, and a simple word-prefix index takes 0.1-0.2 ms per query (245 ms build, ~54 MiB heap). uFuzzy's 162k-phrase benchmark shows ~5 ms per keystroke with 28 MB peak heap. Fuse.js is ~78x slower, and FlexSearch, Orama and MiniSearch keep 67-316 MB of heap. SQLite FTS5 (in Node's built-in node:sqlite, and in the official WASM build at ~0.4 MB gzip) answers in under 1 ms, but a prebuilt DB is 7.5-11.5 MiB brotli. Server-side search (pg_trgm+unaccent, D1/Turso FTS5, Meilisearch from $20/mo, Typesense) works, but every keystroke costs a network round trip plus ops and money.
Pipeline: a daily GitHub Actions cron builds the snapshot using only Node built-ins. It is free for public repos, but runs can start late or be dropped, and schedules switch off after 60 days without repo activity. Publish to Cloudflare R2 (no egress fees) or Workers static assets (free, unlimited requests). Free-tier traps: Workers Free allows 10 ms CPU, D1 Free 5M rows read/day (~25 unindexed scans), Netlify Free 300 credits (15 per deploy). Also: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only, Supabase pauses after 7 idle days, Neon scales to zero, Render spins down, and Fly.io has no free tier.
User data: keep it local-first in IndexedDB via Dexie 4, with persist() and export. Add a thin Hono-on-Workers + D1/Turso last-write-wins sync later. Zero 1.x, Electric and PowerSync are mature, but each needs Postgres with logical replication (or PowerSync's own service) plus a sync server. That is overkill for one user's list. InstantDB Free (1 GB, never paused) is the simplest hosted backend. Safari wipes storage for sites that are not installed after 7 days of Safari use without visiting the site.
Delivery: start with a PWA. iOS 26 opens Home Screen sites as web apps, Web Push works from iOS 16.4 (declarative from 18.4), and Safari has no share_target. Tauri 2.12 desktop builds can start now on this machine (Build Tools 2022, WebView2 155 and Rust 1.99 MSVC checked live). Android needs Android Studio plus the NDK; native iOS needs a Mac.
Versions: Node 24 is maintenance LTS and Node 26 becomes Active LTS today (no corepack from Node 25). TypeScript 7.0.2 has no API until 7.1, so Svelte checks and typed ESLint still need TS 6. Also current: Vite 8.3 (Rolldown), React 19.3, SvelteKit 3.1, Next 16.4, Hono 4.13, Drizzle 0.45 (1.0 still RC), Prisma 7.10 (npm 'latest' points to an 8.0 RC), Biome 2.6, ESLint 10, Vitest 5, Playwright 1.64, pnpm 12.

findings.claim: TypeScript 7.0 (Go-based compiler, released 2026-07-08; npm latest 7.0.2) builds 8-12x faster but ships without a programmatic API until 7.1, so Svelte/Vue/Astro/Angular template checking and typed typescript-eslint still need TypeScript 6.
findings.details: Microsoft blog: 'npm install -D typescript' installs the native tsc. Example: VS Code full build 125.7s -> 10.6s. New defaults: strict on, module esnext, types [], rootDir ./. Deprecated options (target es5, baseUrl, moduleResolution node10) are now hard errors. 'Vue, MDX, Astro, Svelte, and Angular template checking still depend on TypeScript 6.0' because they need the API, expected in 7.1 (7.1.0-beta is already on npm). InfoQ adds that typescript-eslint can't use 7.0 yet. To run both side by side, @typescript/typescript6 provides a 'tsc6' binary. At launch, VS Code support came through a separate extension. Implication: a React+Vite stack can type-check with TS 7 now; a Svelte stack keeps TS 6 for svelte-check.

findings.claim: Vite 8 (released 2026-03-12, now 8.3.5) replaced the esbuild+Rollup pair with the Rust bundler Rolldown and requires Node 20.19+ or 22.12+; React 19.3 shipped on 2026-09-09 and SvelteKit 3 became stable on 2026-10-01.
findings.details: Vite 8 claims 'up to 10-30x faster builds' (Linear's builds went 46s->6s) and adds ~15 MB to install size. @vitejs/plugin-react v6 uses Oxc instead of Babel. Rolldown 1.0 shipped 2026-05-07 (VoidZero). React 19.3 made <ViewTransition> and Fragment Refs stable, with no breaking changes. SvelteKit 3 RC came out 2026-08-13 and Svelte was at 5.57 in Sep 2026. Next.js 16.4 shipped early Oct 2026 (Turbopack is the default). Inference: an offline-first PWA with no SEO needs gets nothing from Next's server features, and Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only, so a Vite SPA (React 19 or Svelte 5, or SvelteKit with the static adapter) is the leaner base.

findings.claim: The Steam games catalog on 2026-10-27 had 196,595 entries; a compact appid+name snapshot is 4.95 MiB raw, 2.44 MiB gzip-9 and 1.80 MiB brotli-11, small enough to send to every client.
findings.details: Source: jsnli/steamappidlist data/games_appid.json (19.9 MB), published daily by GitHub Actions from IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 with a STEAM_KEY. Fields: appid, name, last_modified, price_change_number. DLC is in a separate 8.2 MB file. Names: average 16.7 chars, median 14, p95 35, max 414. 8.1% contain non-ASCII; 12,370 (6.3%) contain CJK or Hangul; 749 have Latin accents; 18 are empty. A JSON [[id,name]] version is 5.70 / 2.52 / 1.82 MiB, and JSON.parse on it took 31 ms. brotli-11 compression took ~8 s, which is fine for a build job. This is a third-party dataset, so production should use your own key.

findings.claim: On this PC, searching all 196,595 accent-folded game names in plain JavaScript takes 6-9 ms per query with a brute-force substring scan and 0.1-0.2 ms with a simple word-prefix inverted index (245 ms to build, ~54 MiB heap).
findings.details: My own script, Node 24.21 / V8 13.6, built-ins only. Normalizing all names (NFKD, strip \p{M}, lowercase, punctuation -> space) took 142 ms and ~11 MiB heap; 'Señor Ñandú: Edición Épica' becomes 'senor nandu edicion epica'. Scan median per query: 'hollow kn' 7.8 ms, 'half life' 8.1 ms, 'senor' 8.4 ms (finds 'Señorita Chupacabra'). Index: 92,569 distinct words; 'the' 1.8 ms, 's' 6.7 ms. Substring hits are noisy ('zelda' matches 'Grizelda'; 'the' gets 25,084 hits), so rank word-prefix matches first and cap results. Not measured on phones; expect several times slower, so run search in a Worker.

findings.claim: In uFuzzy's 162k-phrase benchmark, index-free uFuzzy needed ~5 ms per keystroke and 28 MB peak heap, Fuse.js ~394 ms per keystroke, and the index-based FlexSearch, Orama and MiniSearch retained 316, 192 and 67 MB of heap.
findings.details: Setup: README by the uFuzzy author, Chrome 117, Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U, tested 2023-10, 162,000 phrases (4 MB), 86 searches. Init / total search / peak/retained heap: uFuzzy 0.5 ms / 434 ms (210 ms with prefix caching) / 28.4/7.4 MB. FlexSearch Light 3,210 ms / 83 ms / 670/316 MB. Orama 2,650 / 225 / 313/192. MiniSearch 504 / 1,453 / 438/67. fuzzysort 50 / 1,321 / 175/84. Fuse.js 31 / 33,875 / 245/13.9. Caveats: old library versions, and the author says the test favors uFuzzy's use case. Current npm: uFuzzy 1.0.19 (2025-08), FlexSearch 0.8.212 (2025-09), MiniSearch 7.2.0 (2025-09), Orama 3.1.18 (2025-12), Fuse.js 7.5.0 (2026-07).

findings.claim: Typo tolerance and accent folding differ by library: uFuzzy has latinize() and a SingleError mode but Latin-only regexps by default; FlexSearch 0.8 trades memory for partial matching through tokenize modes and can persist to IndexedDB, SQLite or Postgres; MiniSearch 7.2 offers prefix + fuzzy search and JSON (de)serialization.
findings.details: uFuzzy: no index. intraMode:1 (SingleError) allows one substitution, transposition, insertion or deletion per term. {unicode:true} is '50%-75% slower', which matters because 6.3% of Steam names are CJK/Hangul. FlexSearch 0.8 (Apache-2.0): tokenize strict/forward/reverse/full/tolerant multiply memory by 1, n, 2n-1, n(n-1) and 2(n-2)+2; encoders Normalize and LatinBalance/Advanced/Extra/Soundex; adapters for IndexedDB, Redis, SQLite, Postgres, MongoDB, Clickhouse; async export/import; worker option. The README never says outright that é folds to e. MiniSearch 7.2 (MIT): prefix, fuzzy (edit distance scales with term length), autoSuggest, processTerm, toJSON/loadJSON/loadJSONAsync, discard/vacuum.

findings.topic: SQLite FTS5 on the real catalog (live)
findings.claim: Node 24's built-in node:sqlite (SQLite 3.53.4) includes FTS5. On the real catalog an FTS5 trigram index answers substring queries in 0.14-0.45 ms, but the database is 19.2 MiB (11.5 MiB brotli), 4-6x more to ship than a plain snapshot.
findings.details: node:sqlite is Stability 1.2 (release candidate) since v24.15 and needs no flag. External-content FTS5 over 196,577 names. Trigram with remove_diacritics 1: build 1.5 s, DB 19.2 MiB (gzip 12.5). unicode61 with remove_diacritics 2 and prefix='2 3': build 1.2 s, 14.3 MiB (brotli 7.5); word-prefix MATCH 0.08-0.8 ms, but 'the*' with ORDER BY rank takes 28.6 ms. Unindexed LIKE '%witcher%' takes 21 ms. Gotchas: with detail=none, trigram queries longer than 3 chars throw an error. Per the docs, trigram+remove_diacritics disables indexed LIKE/GLOB, and substrings under 3 chars never match, which affects 2-char CJK words.

findings.topic: SQLite WASM + OPFS in the browser
findings.claim: The official SQLite WASM build (3.54.1-build1) is ~879 KB raw / ~397 KiB gzip and includes FTS5 (with trigram and remove_diacritics) but not FTS3/4. Its 'opfs-sahpool' VFS persists without COOP/COEP headers but allows only one connection per database across tabs by default.
findings.details: I inspected the npm tarball without executing it: 976 KB, and dist/sqlite3.wasm is 879,084 B. Its compile-option strings include ENABLE_FTS5 plus 'trigram' and 'remove_diacritics'. Persistence docs: the 'opfs' VFS must run in a Worker with SharedArrayBuffer, so it needs COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp headers. 'opfs-sahpool' needs neither, works in all major browsers released since March 2023 and is the fastest, but tabs must coordinate with pauseVfs/unpauseVfs (3.50+); before 3.54, multiple same-thread connections could corrupt data. 'opfs-wl' (3.53+) uses Web Locks and needs Atomics.waitAsync. kvvfs is limited to ~5 MB.

findings.claim: PGlite 0.5.12 runs Postgres in the browser or Node (~3 MB gzipped) with pg_trgm, unaccent and fuzzystrmatch bundled as contrib extensions, but has only a single exclusive connection.
findings.details: README: 'only 3mb gzipped'; dual-licensed Apache-2.0 / PostgreSQL License. Extension sizes: pg_trgm 15.8 KB, unaccent 9.1 KB, fuzzystrmatch 11.7 KB; pgvector is a separate package. Persistence: 'idb://name' (IndexedDB) in browsers, a directory in Node, or in-memory. A worker can share one instance across tabs, and there is a live-query extension. Fits as Postgres for local dev and tests without Docker or a native install, or for Electric-style local-first. For a read-only 200k-name catalog it is ~7x heavier than SQLite WASM (~0.4 MB gzip). The base Postgres version is not stated on the pages I read.

findings.claim: PostgreSQL 18 (18.6) is current and 19 is due 2026-11-19. pg_trgm GIN/GiST indexes speed up LIKE/ILIKE and similarity search, but accent-insensitive matching needs unaccent, and indexing it needs an IMMUTABLE wrapper (community practice).
findings.details: PG 19 RC1 was announced 2026-10-15; RC2 is set for 2026-11-12 and GA for 2026-11-19. pg_trgm: gin_trgm_ops and gist_trgm_ops speed up LIKE, ILIKE, ~, ~* and the % operator. Default thresholds: similarity 0.3, word_similarity 0.6, strict 0.5. KNN ordering by 'ORDER BY t <-> q' works only with GiST. Patterns without extractable trigrams fall back to a full-index scan. pg_trgm does not strip accents. The unaccent docs don't state its volatility. Common practice wraps unaccent('unaccent', x) in an IMMUTABLE SQL function so it can be indexed; check provolatile. Locally this needs a native Windows install (no Docker here), PGlite, or a hosted Neon/Supabase.

findings.claim: No permanent free tier was found for Meilisearch Cloud or Typesense Cloud: Meilisearch Cloud starts at $20/month after a 14-day trial, and Typesense Cloud charges a fixed hourly cluster fee even with no traffic.
findings.details: Meilisearch: latest engine 1.55.0 (2026-10-12, endoflife.date); self-hosting is MIT with no usage limits. Its pricing estimator shows usage-based $30/mo (100K docs, 50K searches) or resource-based XS (0.5 vCPU, 1 GB) at $18 plus $5 disk; 14-day trial, no card. Typesense Cloud: hourly fee per configuration plus ~9-12 cents/GB bandwidth (help center). The smallest option is 0.5 GB RAM with 2 vCPUs and a 1 h daily burst. The pricing page didn't render a price; third-party sources say ~$22/mo (unverified). v30.x shipped in 2026, per client-library changelogs. Both give typo tolerance and prefix search, but each keystroke still pays a network round trip.

findings.claim: On Cloudflare's free tier (docs updated 2026-10-12), static assets are free and unlimited (25 MiB per file) and R2 has no egress fees, but Workers Free allows only 10 ms CPU per request or cron run and D1 Free 5M rows read per day.
findings.details: Workers Free: 100,000 requests/day (reset at 00:00 UTC; Error 1027 past it), 10 ms CPU per request and per Cron Trigger, 128 MB memory, 5 cron triggers per account. Static assets: 'free and unlimited', 20,000 files per version, 25 MiB per file. D1 Free: 5M rows read and 100k rows written per day, 5 GB total; FTS5 is supported. R2 Free: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations per month, free egress. Derived: JSON.parse of the 20 MB catalog took 128 ms here, so ingestion can't run in a free Workers cron. An unindexed LIKE over ~196k rows reads ~196k rows, which allows only ~25 searches/day on D1 Free.

findings.claim: Free app-hosting tiers in Oct 2026 have hard catches: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only, Netlify Free's 300 credits/month (15 per production deploy) pause every site once used up, Render Free spins down after 15 minutes idle, and Fly.io has no free tier for new orgs.
findings.details: Vercel Hobby: 'non-commercial personal use only'; per month 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 1M function invocations, 10 GB origin transfer, 4 h Active CPU. Netlify Free: hard limit; bandwidth costs 20 credits/GB and requests 2 credits/10k; deploy previews are free. When credits run out, every site shows 'Site not available', so 30 daily production deploys (450 credits) would exceed it. Render Free: ~1 min to wake, 750 instance-hours/month; free Postgres (1 GB) expires after 30 days plus a 14-day grace period. Fly.io: trial is 2 machine-hours or 7 days; shared-cpu-1x 256 MB costs $2.19/mo. Railway: one-time $5 trial for 30 days, then a $1/mo credit.

findings.claim: Free managed databases in Oct 2026: Neon (1 GB per project, 100 CU-hours, forced scale-to-zero after 5 min), Supabase (500 MB, paused after 1 week of inactivity, 2 projects) and Turso (5 GB, 500M rows read per month, 100 databases).
findings.details: Neon Free: 20 GB total cap across 100 projects; compute is suspended once CU-hours run out; scale-to-zero 'cannot be turned off'; 5 GB egress per project; 10 branches. Supabase Free: 5 GB egress, 1 GB file storage, 50,000 auth MAUs, 2 active projects, 'paused after 1 week of inactivity'; Pro from $25/mo. Turso Free: 10M rows written per month, 3 GB syncs per month, 1-day point-in-time restore; Developer plan $4.99/mo. A personal app used now and then can trip Supabase's pause or Neon's cold starts. D1 and Turso don't mention any pausing on the pages I read.

findings.claim: GitHub Actions scheduled workflows are free on public repos but best-effort: 5-minute minimum interval, delays at the top of each hour, possible dropped runs, and on public repos schedules switch off after 60 days without repo activity.
findings.details: Docs: runs on the default branch, in UTC unless an IANA timezone is set. 'can be delayed during periods of high loads… High load times include the start of every hour'; 'some queued jobs may be dropped'. Free for public repos on standard runners and for self-hosted runners. Private repos on GitHub Free get 2,000 min/month, 500 MB artifacts and 10 GB cache. Jobs run up to 6 h. Observed jitter: jsnli's daily publish commits landed at 03:49, 03:53 and 04:15 UTC on 2026-10-25 to 27. Committing a 19.9 MB file every day bloats git history; GitHub warns above 50 MiB per file, blocks above 100 MiB, and recommends repos under 1 GB.

findings.claim: Zero (1.0 in June 2026, now 1.11.3) and ElectricSQL both need Postgres with logical replication plus a separate sync service, and Electric only syncs reads. PowerSync also needs its own service, and its free cloud projects are deactivated after a week of inactivity.
findings.details: Zero needs Postgres 15+ with wal_level=logical (event triggers recommended) and a zero-cache server run under a supervisor. Neon, RDS and PlanetScale are supported; Supabase, Fly and Render work with caveats. Community reports: 232 KB gzipped client, no SSR. Electric: 'does not do write-path sync', so writes go through your own API. Electric Cloud pay-as-you-go: $1 per million writes, $0.10/GB-month, bills under $5/mo waived (~5M writes); Pro $249/mo. PowerSync (@powersync/web 2.5.0) syncs from Postgres, MongoDB, MySQL or SQL Server. Free tier: 2 GB synced, 500 MB hosted, 50 peak connections. Pro $49/mo. The self-hosted Open Edition uses the FSL, a source-available license that is not OSI open source.

findings.claim: Among lighter local-first options, InstantDB's free tier (1 GB, never paused, commercial use allowed) is the most generous; Dexie Cloud's free tier covers only 3 production users; Replicache is in maintenance mode; and LiveStore, Jazz and TanStack DB are still 0.x.
findings.details: Dexie Cloud Free: 3 production users, 100 MB, 20 requests/s; production costs $0.12 per user per month. InstantDB (@instantdb/react 1.0.67): unlimited API requests, 'never paused'; Pro $30/mo. Triplit: Supabase hired its co-founder on 2025-10-08 but did not merge the product. Replicache: open-sourced and free; users are told to move to Zero. LiveStore 0.5.0 (2026-10-15, Apache-2.0, event sourcing on SQLite). jazz-tools 0.20.19 (2026-07-03). @tanstack/db 0.15.2; persistence via SQLite WASM arrived in 0.6. Inference: for one person's list, Dexie 4 plus per-item updatedAt and soft deletes plus a small sync endpoint feels just as instant, with less lock-in.

findings.claim: In 2026, iOS 26 opens any site added to the Home Screen as a web app by default and supports Web Push for those apps (iOS 16.4+, declarative since 18.4), but Safari still lacks the Web Share Target (share_target) API.
findings.details: iOS/iPadOS 26: an 'Open as web app' toggle in the Add to Home Screen dialog, on by default. Web Push for Home Screen web apps arrived in iOS 16.4; the app must be installed and permission asked from a user gesture. Declarative Web Push (no service worker needed) works in Home Screen apps on iOS/iPadOS 18.4+. MDN marks the share_target manifest member 'Experimental' and 'not Baseline'; in practice it is Chromium-only. So 'share a Steam link into GameAgenda' would work on Android and desktop Chrome/Edge but not on iPhone. Inference: an installed PWA on Windows (Edge/Chrome) already feels like a desktop app without Tauri.

findings.claim: Browser storage is not durable by default: Safari deletes script-writable storage after 7 days of Safari use without interaction (Home Screen web apps keep their own counter), and persist() is granted by heuristics.
findings.details: WebKit 2020-03-24: ITP deletes IndexedDB, localStorage and service-worker registrations/cache 'after seven days of Safari use without user interaction on the site'. Home Screen web apps 'have their own counter of days of use', and WebKit doesn't expect their first-party data to be deleted. Safari 17+ (2023-08-10): each origin can use up to ~60% of disk in browsers and Home Screen apps, 15% inside apps that embed web views. persist() is supported and granted by heuristics, with Home Screen status counting in favour. Chromium: up to 60% of disk per origin. Firefox: best-effort up to 10% of disk or 10 GiB, whichever is smaller; persist() shows a prompt. Back local data with sync or export.

findings.claim: Tauri 2 (CLI 2.12.4) can build Windows desktop apps on this machine today. Android builds also need Android Studio (its bundled JBR serves as JAVA_HOME), the SDK/NDK and Rust Android targets, and iOS builds require macOS with Xcode.

findings.claim: For tooling: ESLint 10 accepts only flat config and its typed rules can't use TypeScript 7.0; Biome 2.6 lints and formats without tsc; pnpm 12 is current; Drizzle 1.0 is still an RC; and npm's 'latest' tag for prisma currently installs 8.0.0-rc.28 instead of the stable 7.10.1.
findings.details: ESLint 10.0.0 (Feb 2026) dropped eslintrc, and ESLint 9 reached end of life on 2026-08-06; latest is 10.13.0. Biome 2.6.3 has type-aware rules that don't depend on tsc. Vitest 5.0 shipped around late Aug 2026 (releases.sh; now 5.0.5); Playwright is at 1.64.1. pnpm 12.15 is marked 'Latest' on GitHub (12.16.1 on 2026-10-27). For a solo repo, npm workspaces are enough and Turborepo 2.11 isn't needed. Drizzle 0.45.4 is the stable line; 1.0.0-rc.5 is under the rc tag. GitHub marks Prisma 7.10.1 as 'Latest' and every 8.0 build as a pre-release, yet the npm 'latest' tag points to 8.0.0-rc.28 (seen 2026-10-28). Pin versions.

recommendations: Run all search on the device. Each day, publish a versioned 'appid<TAB>name' snapshot (~1.8 MiB brotli / 2.4 MiB gzip for 196.6k games) plus a small manifest. Cache the snapshot in the Cache API or OPFS and refresh it when the version changes. In a Web Worker, build an accent-folded word-prefix index (sub-ms queries). Fall back to a substring scan for CJK names and very short queries, and use uFuzzy SingleError only when a query returns nothing (for typos). Do not use Fuse.js, and do not ship a SQLite FTS5 file to phones (7.5-11.5 MiB).

Ingestion: a GitHub Actions cron at an odd minute (e.g. '17 3 * * *') plus workflow_dispatch, running a Node 24 script with no dependencies (fetch + zlib brotli; node:sqlite if you also want a server DB). Keep STEAM_KEY and a Cloudflare API token as secrets. Publish to Cloudflare R2 or Workers static assets, not into git history. Use a public repo (free minutes) and keep it active (60-day rule).

Frontend: a Vite 8 SPA/PWA, either React 19.3 with TanStack Virtual for long result lists, or Svelte 5/SvelteKit 3 with the static adapter. Skip Next.js server features. Use TypeScript 7.0 for React; keep TS 6 if you pick Svelte (svelte-check) or type-aware ESLint until TS 7.1.

Store the user's lists on the device first: Dexie 4 (IndexedDB) with liveQuery. One record per appid, with status flags (quiero jugar / comprado / completado / platinado), addedAt, updatedAt and a deleted flag. Call navigator.storage.persist() and add JSON export/import from v1 so data survives Safari eviction.

Sync in phase 2: a thin Hono 4 API on Cloudflare Workers + D1 (or Turso) using last-write-wins per record on updatedAt; personal use fits the free limits. If you'd rather use a hosted backend, InstantDB Free is never paused; Supabase Free pauses after 7 idle days. Use Zero, Electric or PowerSync only if you later need real-time multi-user features.

Delivery order: PWA first (installable on Windows via Edge/Chrome, Android, and the iPhone Home Screen; iOS 26 opens it as a web app). Then Tauri 2 desktop, whose prerequisites are already on this machine. Android via Tauri or Capacitor after installing Android Studio and the NDK. Native iOS only if a Mac is available, or by rewriting the UI in Expo to use EAS cloud builds.

Hosting: serve the app and snapshot from Cloudflare Workers static assets or R2 (free, unlimited static requests, no egress fees). Avoid Netlify Free for daily deploys (15 credits each, 300 hard cap), avoid Vercel Hobby if there is any monetization, and don't run ingestion in a free Workers cron (10 ms CPU).

Tooling on this PC: stay on Node 24.21 for now (supported until 2028-04-30) and plan a move to Node 26 later. Use npm 11, or 'corepack enable pnpm' while on Node 24. Biome 2.6 for lint+format, Vitest 5 and Playwright 1.64 for tests. Pin exact ORM versions if you need one (Prisma's npm 'latest' is an RC; Drizzle 1.0 is still RC).

If you prefer classic server-side search: Postgres 18 with pg_trgm GIN and an IMMUTABLE unaccent wrapper (expect Neon cold starts), or D1/Turso FTS5 with the trigram tokenizer and remove_diacritics, behind Hono. Use PGlite or node:sqlite for local development instead of installing Postgres or Docker. Meilisearch and Typesense aren't worth $20+/mo for 200k short names.

Early on, measure on the real target phone with the real snapshot: download, parse, normalize, index build and per-keystroke time. Set budgets such as under 50 ms per keystroke, under 100 MB heap, and under 1.5 s from cold start to first search.
risks: The catalog depends on IStoreService, which needs a Steam Web API key (the keyless GetAppList v2 returns 404). The jsnli dataset is third-party and unofficial, so production should use your own key and handle its terms and rate limits.
Phones run JavaScript several times slower than this desktop (not measured). Index-based libraries can use 67-316 MB of heap on catalogs this size, which risks tab crashes on low-end Android or iOS.
Safari ITP deletes IndexedDB/OPFS data for sites that are not installed after 7 days of Safari use without visiting them. Without sync or export, users can lose their lists.
GitHub schedules can start late or be dropped, and they switch off after 60 days without activity on public repos. Without retries and a staleness check, the snapshot can silently go out of date.

Free tiers and policies change: Netlify moved to credits, Vercel Hobby is non-commercial, Supabase pauses idle projects, PowerSync deactivates them, Fly.io dropped its free tier, and GitHub announced a self-hosted runner fee (Dec 2025) and then postponed it.
Libraries still in pre-release or churn: Drizzle 1.0 RC, Prisma 8 RC on npm 'latest', TanStack DB 0.15, LiveStore 0.5, Jazz 0.20, Tauri 3 alphas, TS 7.0 without an API. Expect breaking changes.
6.3% of game names are CJK/Hangul. Word tokenizers and FTS5 trigram (minimum 3 chars) handle short CJK queries poorly unless there is a substring fallback.
Tauri mobile has reported rough edges, and building for iOS natively (Tauri or Capacitor) requires macOS/Xcode, which this Windows-only setup can't provide.
Version and date facts are moving right now: Node 26 Active LTS starts today, PostgreSQL 19 GA is due 2026-11-19, Capacitor 9 at end of Nov 2026, and CocoaPods trunk goes read-only on 2026-12-02.
open_questions: Is the app strictly personal (one user, several devices), or will lists be shared or social? That decides between simple last-write-wins sync and a real sync engine.
Which phone does the user target (iPhone or Android), and is a Mac available? That decides whether native iOS is realistic or whether to stay with a PWA on iOS.
Should the catalog include DLC, software, demos and soundtracks, or games only? The DLC list alone is another 8.2 MB of JSON.
Will the app be commercial in any way (ads, donations, paid)? That affects Vercel Hobby and other non-commercial free tiers.
Are cover images needed offline? Caching Steam capsules for a whole backlog changes storage and bandwidth budgets.
How does Cloudflare D1 count 'rows read' for FTS5 MATCH queries? It wasn't documented on the pages reviewed, and it matters if search moves to D1.
What are the real per-keystroke latency and memory on the user's actual phone for the chosen search approach? Only desktop numbers were measured.
Which authentication method suits the sync phase (e.g. Supabase Auth's 50k MAU free, Steam OpenID, or passkeys)? Auth was not evaluated in this dimension.

verdicts.correction: Steam's renamed tab does not strictly mean 'all achievements'. Valve (2026-10-15): 'The Perfect Games tab is now called Completed and expands to show both completed games and games with completed achievement sets', so games with only one completed set also appear. DLC achievements are left out of overall progress 'until you have access to the content', which means access, not strictly ownership. Backloggd's 'Completed' = 'Beat your main objective' comes from its status tooltip; the cited /about page does not define it. The rest holds. LaunchBox's defaults are Not Started (Unplayed, Want to Play, Won't Play), Active (In Progress, Continuous, Paused) and Done (Beaten, Completed, Mastered, Dropped). Its rules map RA beaten to Beaten, all RA softcore achievements to Completed, and all achievements (RA hardcore) to Mastered, so Beaten < Completed < Mastered. Platinum normally excludes DLC trophies, with exceptions.
verdicts.evidence: ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp (appid 593110) dates the post 'Steam Achievement Sets Now in Beta' to 2026-10-15T22:06:30Z. Its full text confirms the Completed-tab sentence, base-game vs DLC sets, a 'set complete' trophy that is kept when achievements are added later, and archived achievements that don't 'block their progress'. Backloggd's tooltip text appears on profile pages (v1.17.5). The LaunchBox featurebase article lists the values and rules. Secondary sources on the Platinum DLC rule cite exceptions, for example Life is Strange: Before the Storm. The Giant Bomb page returned 403.

This is a design recommendation, so only its factual anchors can be checked, and they hold. All four cited apps share the 5 proposed states as a common subset, but none of them stops at 5. Playnite GameDatabase.cs defaults: 'Not Played','Played','Beaten','Completed','Playing','Abandoned','On Hold','Plan to Play' (8). LaunchBox has 10 values in 3 groups. IGN Playlist: wishlists, backlog, playing, paused, beat, quit. Playlogged: Backlog, Playing, Completed, Dropped, Wishlist, plus Paused (v1.3.1). Backloggd keeps Ownership/Library entries separate from the played status, and Steam keeps the wishlist apart from the library.

This is also a design recommendation, and its factual anchors hold. Playnite sets DefaultStatus='Not Played' for new games. It assigns PlayedStatus='Played' on import when playtime > 0 (GameDatabase.cs), and when a game starts running if its status is empty or the default (GamesEditor.cs, around lines 1352-1364, with a 'Do nothing' option). LaunchBox applies automatic rules: playtime or any achievement gives In Progress, RA beaten gives Beaten, and all achievements give Mastered; the lower rule wins. dynamicdonut (2024-01-01) says Infinite Backlog can 'feel too much like homework sometimes'. The specific GameAgenda rules (date stamps, undo, Platinado implies Completado) are new design choices; neither app does them verbatim.

additional_findings.claim: Steam's keyless store and API endpoints send no CORS headers, so a browser-only PWA cannot read them with fetch(); Steam data has to come from a prebuilt snapshot, your own proxy or edge function, or native HTTP.
additional_findings.details: Live test 2026-10-28 with 'Origin: https://gameagenda.example': store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails, /api/storesearch, /search/suggest and api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1 all returned HTTP 200 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, or any Access-Control-* header. Options: ship the catalog as a static file built in CI, add a small proxy or edge function, or use native HTTP (Tauri http plugin, Capacitor native HTTP). Images on shared.akamai.steamstatic.com still load in tags without CORS. One sample per endpoint.

additional_findings.topic: Steam Web API key requirements and terms
additional_findings.claim: The full app list needs a Steam Web API key, which a limited Steam account (under $5 USD spent) cannot use, which must be kept confidential and so cannot ship in the client, and which is capped at 100,000 calls/day.
additional_findings.details: Steamworks docs: IStoreService/GetAppList requires 'key' ('Any web API key'). Steam Support (Limited User Accounts): 'Accessing the Steam Web API' is restricted until the account has spent at least $5.00 USD in the store. Steam Web API Terms (last updated July 2010): 100,000 calls per day; keep the key confidential; Steam Data may go to end users for their personal use; nothing may imply Valve endorsement. Keys are requested at steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey. So the catalog refresh must run server-side or in CI with the key stored as a secret.

additional_findings.claim: IStoreService/GetAppList returns at most 50,000 apps per call (default 10,000), pages with last_appid, returns only games by default, and accepts if_modified_since for incremental refreshes.
additional_findings.details: Parameters in the Steamworks docs: key, if_modified_since ('Return only items that have been modified since this date'), have_description_language, include_games (on by default), include_dlc, include_software, include_videos, include_hardware, last_appid ('For continuations'), max_results ('Default 10k, max 50k'). jsnli's index.js loops on response.have_more_results and last_appid with max_results=50000, so 196,595 games take about 4 calls. A daily job could fetch only changes with if_modified_since and patch the snapshot. Not live-tested, since I have no key.

additional_findings.claim: The games-only GetAppList feed already leaves out soundtracks and DLC, so a 'show only games' filter comes free from the data source. The 'Demo'-named entries left in it are real game-type apps.
additional_findings.details: In the 2026-10-27 games file, Hollow Knight (367520) and Silksong (1030300) are present. Soundtracks 598190 and 3928720 and DLC 916000, which storesearch and suggest return for 'hollow knight', are absent. Of the 71 names containing 'Demo', I checked 40 with GetItems and all were type 0 (game), so a type filter won't hide them. storesearch labels every item 'app'; GetItems exposes a numeric type (0 = game and 11 = soundtrack seen).

additional_findings.claim: Keyless IStoreBrowseService/GetItems accepted 100 appids in one call, so covers and descriptions can be fetched in batches rather than one request per game.
additional_findings.details: Live test: 100 appids in one input_json returned HTTP 200, 32,658 B, in 0.31 s, with 100/100 success. A detailed call returned type, name and hashed asset paths (header '7983574d.../header.jpg', asset_url_format 'steam/apps/1030300/${FILENAME}?t=...'). The legacy URL .../store_item_assets/steam/apps/1030300/header.jpg also returned 200. At 100 per call, about 1,966 calls cover every game. The maximum batch size, rate limits and keyless terms are undocumented and were not probed. Responses carry no CORS headers (see X1).

additional_findings.topic: Licensing and size of the jsnli dataset
additional_findings.claim: jsnli/steamappidlist has no license and its git history is already about 462 MiB, so it is fine for a prototype but not as a production dependency.
additional_findings.details: GitHub API: license null, 57 stars, created 2023-04-16, repo size 472,914 KB. The size comes from daily commits that rewrite a 19.9 MB games file plus an 8.2 MB DLC file. With no license, the repo grants no right to reuse or redistribute its files, and it depends on one person's key and their Actions workflow (generate.yml). For production, run your own GetAppList job and publish the snapshot as a release asset, an R2 object or a static asset instead of committing it to git every day.

additional_findings.claim: Steam game names change and contain special characters, so saved entries must be keyed by appid, and names refreshed and normalized from the daily list.
additional_findings.details: Live test: appid 292030 is now 'The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered' (with an em dash) in both the 2026-10-27 GetAppList snapshot and appdetails with l=spanish. 985 of 196,595 names contain ®, ™ or ©, and 15,830 (8.1%) contain non-ASCII characters. Store each entry as appid plus a name snapshot for offline display, refresh names from the daily list, and fold dashes and symbols when normalizing. In my test, NFKD plus mark stripping plus mapping punctuation to spaces turned 'Señor Ñandú: Edición Épica' into 'senor nandu edicion epica'.
